Lay the tortillas on a flat surface. Lay the lettuce leaves on the tortilla, leaving about 1 inch of the outside of the tortilla uncovered.
Divide the chicken between the tortillas and spread it over the lettuce.
Sprinkle the feta cheese on top of the chicken and add the red pepper strips and tomato slices.

Fold two opposite sides of the tortilla in about 1 inch. Take one of the other sides and roll it toward the other side making a tight roll. Be careful to keep the filling from spilling out. Cut the rolled wrap in half.
Serve with a side salad if desired.

title: Salmon and Wheat Berry Pesto Salad
description: Wheat berries are the kernel of the wheat plant with the outer husk removed. They have a nutty flavor and chewy texture and are filled with fiber, protein, and iron. You can make a batch of these ahead of time and store them in your refrigerator for up to a week. If you can’t find wheat berries, either farro, spelt, or brown rice can be substituted in this recipe.
serving_size: 2 1/4 cups of salad mix and vegetables + 3 oz. salmon
nutrients_raw: Calories 350; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 430mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 35g 13%; Dietary Fiber 8g 29%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 27g; Potassium 790mg 17%
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a sheet pan with aluminum foil and spray lightly with cooking spray.
Cook the wheat berries according to their package directions.

Brush each of the salmon fillets with half a teaspoon of pesto. Place on the prepared sheet pan and place in the oven. Cook until the salmon reaches 145 degrees F, about 15–20 minutes depending on the thickness of the salmon fillet.
When the wheat berries are cooked, drain them and toss them with 4 1/2 teaspoons of pesto.
Divide the spinach and arugula between 2 large plates or bowls. Toss in the wheat berries to coat the greens with pesto.
Place 1 salmon fillet on top of each plate of greens. Add half the green beans and tomatoes and sprinkle each bowl with pine nuts and microgreens.

title: Baked Tilapia with Roasted Veggies
description: Tilapia is a mild and light white fish that cooks quickly and is easily found in most grocery stores. With tomatoes, vegetables, and herbs, the fish pulls in all those Mediterranean flavors as it cooks.
nutrients_raw: Calories 260; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 230mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 33g; Potassium 1190mg 25%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) cans fire-roasted tomatoes (no salt added)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
If necessary, cut the fish into 4 pieces and season it on both sides with pepper. Set aside.

In a large oven-safe sauté pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 3 minutes, until just starting to soften. If you don’t have a large oven-safe sauté pan, more the fish and veggies onto a sheet pan or casserole to cook in the oven.
Add the eggplant to the onion and sauté for 3 minutes, until just starting to soften.
Add zucchini, peppers, tomatoes, oregano, salt, and garlic powder and mix well.
Nestle the fish fillets into the tomato and vegetable mixture.
Cover the pan and place it in the oven. Bake for 15 minutes until the vegetables and fish are cooked through.

title: Southwest Breakfast Tostadas with Black Beans & Spinach
description: These southwest breakfast tostadas are layered with spiced black beans, sautéed spinach, and an egg for a great start to your day. Crisp corn tortillas provide a whole grain base, while fiber-rich beans and healthy fats from avocado help support blood glucose (blood sugar) management. It’s a bold vegetarian breakfast that fits well into a diabetes-friendly eating plan.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 12g; Potassium 550mg 12%
ingredients: 1 cup no-salt-added black beans (rinsed and drained)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Place the corn tortillas on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Lightly spray both sides with cooking spray. Bake for 6–7 minutes on each side or until they become crispy and golden brown. Remove from the oven and set aside.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, combine the black beans, garlic clove, water, chili powder, ground cumin, and salt.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until heated through. Using a fork or potato masher, mash the beans to create a spreadable consistency. Remove from the heat and set aside.​
In a large nonstick skillet, heat 1 teaspoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the spinach and salt. Cook, stirring frequently, until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.

In the same skillet, heat the remaining 1 teaspoon of olive oil over medium heat.​ Crack the eggs into the skillet, spacing them evenly. Cook the eggs to your desired doneness (e.g., sunny side up or over easy).

To assemble, spread an even layer of the black bean mixture over each baked tortilla.​ Top with sautéed spinach, followed by a cooked egg and tomatoes.​ Add slices of avocado and sprinkle with fresh cilantro leaves.

title: Italian Beans and Greens Salad
description: Beans and greens is a classic Italian meal or side dish. In this diabetes-friendly version, the cured ham is replaced with turkey bacon and chicken sausage. They are mixed with baby greens and cannellini beans and made into a salad. It’s a hearty, fresh twist on a mediterranean classic.
serving_size: 1 cup salad greens + 1 oz. chicken sausage
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 15mg 5%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 410mg 9%
ingredients: 2 slice turkey bacon (cut into ½ inch pieces)
2 whole Italian seasoned chicken sausages (cut into ½ -inch rounds)
1/2 cup low sodium cannellini beans (rinsed and drained)
steps: In a large skillet, cook the turkey bacon until crispy and sausage until browned.
Place greens, cannellini beans, and onions in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, garlic, and black pepper together. Drizzle over the salad and toss to coat the greens. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.

title: Mediterranean Chopped Jar Salad
description: A perfect way to prep lunch ahead of time and make sure you have a nourishing lunch ready to go! Place the dressing on the bottom of the jar and layer the ingredients on top. Top it off with salad greens or pack them on their own to keep them fresher. These colorful jars will make your mouth water!
serving_size: 2 cups lettuce + 2 cups salad mix (including 2 oz chicken)
nutrients_raw: Calories 290; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 24g 9%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 29g; Potassium 800mg 17%
steps: Set out 2 12–16 oz. mason jars and lids. In a small bowl, whisk the Tzatziki dressing ingredients together (¼ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt; 2 T. diced cucumber; 1/8 teaspoon dried oregano; 1 ½ tablespoons lemon juice and 1/8 teaspoon kosher salt. The dressing will be divided between the two jars.

Assemble your jars. Divide the chicken between the jars and place it on top of with 2.5 Tablespoons Tzatziki dressing in each jar. Add half the red pepper, cucumber, onion, cauliflower, tomatoes, chickpeas, and feta cheese to each jar.
If there is room, add the torn lettuce on top, or pack it separately in a resealable bag. Seal both jars tightly until you are ready to use them.
Store the jars in the refrigerator. They will last for 3–4 days when sealed tightly.

title: Pasta Primavera with Chickpea Pasta
description: You get a boost of protein and fiber with chickpea pasta. Filled with fresh veggies, this hearty and flavorful dish is an easy spring or summer meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 350; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 57g 21%; Dietary Fiber 13g 46%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 20g; Potassium 1180mg 25%
ingredients: 1/2 cup red onion (sliced, about ½ a small onion)
1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes (no salt added)
1 (15 ounce) can cannellini beans (no added salt, rinsed and drained)
steps: Heat olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add onion and peppers and sauté for 3 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook for another minute.
Add broccoli, carrots, asparagus, zucchini, basil, oregano, and pepper and sauté for 1 minute, until the spices are fragrant.
Add the vegetable broth and tomatoes. Cook for 5–7 minutes, until the liquid is reduced by half. Stir in the cannellini beans and keep warm.
While the vegetables are cooking, boil the pasta following the package instructions, until al dente. Drain and mix into the vegetable mixture.
Serve with shaved parmesan cheese if desired.

title: Mediterranean Spinach & Feta Egg Bites
description: Fluffy baked egg bites made with eggs, spinach, tomato, and feta for a protein-packed, low-carb breakfast. These savory bites deliver satisfying flavor while staying light and portable, making them a smart option for any morning.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 215mg 72%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 250mg 5%
ingredients: 1 medium tomato Tomato (seeded and finely diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease or line a 12-cup silicone muffin pan.

Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add spinach and cook for 3–4 minutes until wilted and most of the liquid has evaporated. You should end up with ~1 cup (150 g) cooked spinach. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, black pepper, and oregano (if using) until smooth.
Divide the spinach evenly among muffin cups. Top each with diced tomato and a sprinkle of feta. Pour egg mixture over the spinach and tomato, filling each cup about ¾ full.
Bake for 22–25 minutes, or until the eggs are puffed and set in the center.
Let them rest for 5 minutes before removing from the pan. Serve warm or refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat gently in the microwave.

title: Baked Blueberry Almond Oatmeal
description: A hearty baked oatmeal made with oats, chia, flax, and hemp seeds, folded with blueberries and topped with non-fat Greek yogurt and toasted almonds. This fiber- and protein-rich breakfast offers balanced nutrition with heart-healthy fats and no added sugars.
nutrients_raw: Calories 250; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 170mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 15g; Potassium 320mg 7%
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease or line a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Spread the almonds on a rimmed baking sheet. Toast in the oven for 5–8 minutes, until lightly browned and fragrant.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, almond milk, vanilla, and sugar free brown sugar alternative until smooth and creamy.
In a large bowl, stir together the chia seeds, flaxseed, rolled oats, hemp hearts, almond flour, cinnamon, baking powder, and salt.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until fully combined. The batter will thicken slightly as the chia and flax seeds absorb the liquid.
Gently fold in the blueberries.
Spread the mixture evenly in the prepared loaf pan. Bake for 30–35 minutes, turning the pan halfway through, until the center is set and the top is lightly golden and beginning to crack.

Let the oatmeal cool for 10 minutes before slicing into 6 equal portions. Serve warm, topped with ¼ cup low-fat Greek yogurt and 1 tablespoon slivered almonds per serving. Wrap cooled leftovers and store in the refrigerator.

title: Moroccan-Spiced Cod with Carrot Ribbons
description: This Moroccan-spiced cod is infused with warm, fragrant spices and paired with tender carrot ribbons for a light yet satisfying meal. Roasting the carrots under the fish adds flavor while keeping the dish simple and streamlined. It's a nutrient-rich, low-carb, very-low-carb, and low-fat meal option ideal for people living with diabetes looking for something vibrant.
serving_size: 4 oz cod and 1 cup carrot ribbons
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 480mg 10%
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix the cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Rub the spice mixture over the cod fillets. Set aside.
Toss the carrot ribbons with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on the baking sheet and place cod fillets on top.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, or until the cod flakes easily with a fork and the carrots are tender-crisp.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and sprinkle of fresh herbs before serving.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken with Brussels Sprouts and Apple
description: This low-fat sheet pan dinner brings together juicy chicken, roasted Brussels sprouts, and sweet apples for a balanced mix of savory and naturally sweet flavors. The simple mustard vinaigrette ties it all together without the need for heavy sauces. With lean protein, fiber, and ingredients with minimal added sugar, it’s a wholesome, diabetes-friendly meal made easy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 240mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 27g; Potassium 620mg 13%
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into halves or large chunks)
1 med apple ([like Honeycrisp or Fuji], cored and diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, thyme, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken, Brussels sprouts, apple slices, and red onion. Drizzle with the marinade and toss to coat.

Spread everything evenly on the baking sheet. Roast for 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F internal temperature) and Brussels sprouts are tender and golden.
Serve warm, garnished with a squeeze of lemon.

title: Spaghetti Squash Stir-Fry with Chicken & Veggies
description: This colorful stir-fry swaps noodles for roasted spaghetti squash, creating a lower carb base that’s still hearty and satisfying. Paired with lean chicken breast and a medley of crisp vegetables, it’s finished with a savory-sweet sesame soy sauce for balanced flavor. With plenty of fiber and protein, it’s a diabetes-friendly meal that doesn’t sacrifice taste.
nutrients_raw: Calories 310; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 36g 13%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 11g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 31g; Potassium 900mg 19%
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Cut the squash in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet and roast until tender, 30–40 min. Let it cool slightly, then shred into strands with a fork.

While the squash roasts, heat 1 tsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, season lightly with black pepper, and cook until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining teaspoon of olive oil to the skillet. Stir in the garlic, cabbage, bell pepper, and carrots. Cook for 3–5 minutes, until just tender but still crisp.
Return the chicken to the skillet along with the spaghetti squash strands and green onions. Drizzle in soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Toss to combine and heat through.
Divide among bowls and garnish with chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.

title: Power Oats Mug Muffin
description: In the mood for a warm, comforting low carb treat that you can make in 5 minutes? Try this Power Oats Mug Muffin as a tasty option for breakfast or dessert.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 165mg 55%; Sodium 80mg 3%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 12g; Potassium 190mg 4%
ingredients: 2 tbsp oat flour (blend regular oats, if you don’t have oat flour on hand)
steps: In a small bowl or mug, whisk together the Greek yogurt, egg, and vanilla extract.
Add the oat flour and baking powder. Mix until smooth.
Stir in the cinnamon and blueberries.
Microwave on high for 1 minute and 30 seconds to 2 minutes, or until the muffin is puffed and set. Cooking time may vary based on your microwave.

title: Turkey and Veggie Stir-Fry
description: This turkey and veggie stir-fry is a colorful, nutrient-dense meal that’s big on flavor and balanced in nutrition. Lean ground turkey, vibrant vegetables, and a tangy-sweet sauce come together over a bed of hearty brown rice. With a smart mix of protein, fiber, and healthy fats, it’s a great option for blood glucose (blood sugar) stability and diabetes-friendly eating. This is a DASH (Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension) and low carb recipe.
serving_size: 3 oz turkey, 1 cup veggies, 1/2 cup rice
nutrients_raw: Calories 380; Total Fat 16g 21%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 40mg 13%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 35g 13%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 25g; Potassium 644mg 14%
ingredients: 1 tbsp sugar-free maple syrup with monk fruit
steps: In a small bowl, mix 2 Tbsp coconut aminos, 1 Tbsp avocado oil, 1 Tbsp sugar-free maple syrup, 1 Tbsp lime juice, and 1 pinch chili flakes until combined. Set aside.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat and add 2 Tbsp avocado oil. Once hot, stir in the ground turkey and chopped garlic. Cook while stirring occasionally until the turkey is browned and cooked through, about 8–10 minutes.
Add zucchini and carrots to the turkey mixture. Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring to combine. Add kale and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until it begins to soften.
Pour the prepared stir-fry sauce over the mixture and stir well. Cook for another 2 minutes to ensure everything is evenly coated and the kale is fully wilted.
Serve the stir-fry over rice and sprinkle peanuts on top for a crunchy garnish.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Soy-Glazed Mushrooms and Veggie Brown Rice
description: This balanced salmon dish pairs crispy pan-seared filets with savory soy-glazed mushrooms and a veggie-loaded brown rice pilaf. The mix of heart-healthy fats, fiber-rich whole grains, and antioxidant-packed vegetables makes it both satisfying and nourishing. With smart seasoning and no added sugar, it's a blood glucose (blood sugar)-friendly option for people with diabetes looking for a flavorful, well-rounded meal. This is a DASH (Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension) and low-fat recipe.
nutrients_raw: Calories 330; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 41g 15%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 25g; Potassium 1166mg 25%
steps: Preheat the skillet over medium heat. Once the pan is hot, add 1 tsp oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and 1/4 tsp black pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3–4 minutes.
Add rice and spinach to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until the rice is warmed through and spinach has wilted, 2–3 minutes. Cover and set aside.
Preheat another medium skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat fillets dry with paper towels and place skin-side down on a plate; season the top side with 1/4 tsp garlic powder and 1/4 tsp black pepper.

Once the skillet is hot, add 1 tsp oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add salmon, skin-side down, and cook, flipping once, until skin is crispy and flesh is opaque, 3–4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for next step).

Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium-high heat; add remaining 1 tsp oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add mushrooms and 2 garlic cloves; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4–5 minutes.
Add soy sauce to the skillet and continue to cook until the liquid has evaporated, 1–2 minutes more; remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice, salmon, and mushrooms between plates.

title: Hearty Breakfast Frittata
description: Frittatas are a great way to use up extra vegetables before they go bad. Using whatever you have on hand, a variety of non-starchy vegetables helps keep the carb content low and feelings of fullness high.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 95mg 32%; Sodium 270mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 390mg 8%
ingredients: 2 cup kale (chopped, cut into small pieces)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Spray an 8- x 8-inch baking pan with cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs and egg substitute until well combined. Add in cottage cheese and yogurt and whisk to combine. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add onion and red pepper and sauté for 3 minutes, until vegetables begin to soften. Add garlic and sauté for another minute.
Stir in spinach, kale, and broccoli, and cook to wilt the greens, about 2 minutes. Add the artichokes, red pepper flakes, and dried basil. Remove from heat.
Spread the vegetables in the bottom of the prepared pan. Pour the egg and cheese mixture over the vegetables and make sure they are covered well.
Place the pan in the middle of the oven and bake for 40–45 minutes, or until the mixture is set and doesn’t jiggle when lightly shaken.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes, then cut into 6 pieces. Garnish with fresh basil if desired.

title: Cheesy Eggplant Rollatini
description: This lighter eggplant rollatini delivers classic Italian comfort with fewer carbohydrates and less saturated fat than traditional eggplant parmesan. Thinly sliced eggplant is roasted instead of breaded, then filled with a savory mixture of ricotta, mozzarella, and sautéed kale, onion, and garlic for added fiber and flavor. The result is a diabetes-friendly, vegetarian main dish that fits well into a low-fat eating pattern while still feeling hearty and satisfying.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 15mg 5%; Sodium 90mg 4%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 9g; Potassium 750mg 16%
ingredients: 2 med eggplant (about 2 lb total, sliced lengthwise into 1/4-inch-thick strips. You should have 18 strips.)
1 small yellow onion (about 4 oz, finely chopped)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Arrange the eggplant slices in a single layer on two rimmed baking sheets. Lightly coat both sides with olive oil cooking spray. Roast for 18–22 minutes, flipping halfway, until tender and pliable. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.

Heat the remaining 1/2 tsp of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the kale and cook, stirring, for 3–4 minutes, until fully wilted and any moisture has cooked off. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
In a medium bowl, combine the ricotta, mozzarella, Greek yogurt, black pepper, and Italian seasoning. Stir in the cooled kale mixture until evenly incorporated.

Spread 2 cups of crushed tomatoes evenly in the bottom of a 9 X 13-inch baking dish. Place 1/4 cup of filling at one end of each eggplant slice and roll up nice and snug. Arrange seam-side down in the baking dish on top of the tomatoes.

Cover loosely with foil and bake at 375 degrees F for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake an additional 20-25 minutes, until the eggplant starts to brown and the tomato sauce is lightly bubbling. Sprinkle with crushed red pepper flakes, if using.
Let the dish stand for 5 minutes before serving. Top with the torn basil and divide into 6 servings, with 3 rollatini per plate and sauce spooned over the top.

title: Whole Wheat Penne with Mushrooms & Kale
description: This earthy whole wheat penne dish is packed with sautéed mushrooms, tender kale, and a light Parmesan finish for a comforting yet wholesome meal. Whole grain pasta and leafy greens bring fiber and nutrients to the table, helping slow digestion and support steady blood glucose (blood sugar). It’s a balanced, plant-forward option that fits easily into a diabetes-friendly eating plan. This is a DASH (Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension) and mediterranean recipe.
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 53g 19%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 14g; Potassium 730mg 16%
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add pasta and cook until al dente, according to package directions. Reserve ½ cup of the pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in garlic, red pepper flakes (if using), salt, and black pepper. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add kale and vegetable broth, stirring occasionally, until the greens are tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and add the drained pasta to the skillet. Toss everything together, adding a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to coat the noodles evenly.
Remove from heat, stir in Parmesan cheese and lemon juice, and toss again.

title: Crispy Potato Taco Bowl
description: This taco bowl features a hearty base of roasted white potatoes and fluffy cauliflower rice topped with savory ground beef, mushrooms, and red bell peppers. Fresh lime juice and cilantro brighten every bite, while creamy avocado adds richness and balance. It’s a satisfying, veggie-packed, high-fiber twist on classic taco flavors that’s easy enough for weeknights and perfect for build-your-own bowls.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 30mg 10%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 31g 11%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 1090mg 23%
ingredients: 12 oz white potatoes (about 2 medium, diced into 1/2-inch cubes)
1 cup red bell pepper (about 1 medium pepper, diced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Toss diced potatoes with 1 1/2 tsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp black pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 20–25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until tender and lightly browned.

In the same skillet, heat the remaining 1 1/2 tsp olive oil over medium heat. Add ground beef, chopped mushrooms, and diced red bell pepper. Cook for 8–10 minutes, breaking apart the beef, until meat is fully cooked and vegetables are tender.

Stir in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Add the tomato sauce and water and bring to a simmer. Bring to a boil then reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the liquid is reduced. Remove from heat.

While the beef mixture is simmering, heat cauliflower rice in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally until heated through. Add the cilantro and lime juice and mix together. Keep warm until ready to serve.
Divide the cauliflower rice evenly among four bowls. Top each bowl evenly with roasted potatoes, beef-mushroom-pepper mixture, two tomatoes, and 1/4 of a sliced avocado.

title: Falafel Salad with Lemon-Herb Vinaigrette
description: This salad is loaded with crisp veggies, warm herb-packed chickpea patties (falafel), and a zesty lemon vinaigrette for a satisfying meal. Baked instead of fried, the falafel keeps things lighter while still delivering fiber and plant-based protein. With no added sugar and plenty of carbs that will digest slowly, it's a diabetes-friendly option for a hearty lunch or dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 8g 29%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 720mg 15%
ingredients: 1 cup canned chickpeas (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.

Place chickpeas in a food processor with 1 small yellow onion, 2 cloves garlic, herbs and spices (1 cup fresh parsley leaves, 1 cup fresh cilantro leaves, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp black pepper). Pulse until the mixture is coarse and holds together when pressed.
Add baking powder and flour, pulsing briefly to combine. Chill for at least 1 hour.
Form into small balls or patties (about 1–1.5 inches wide). Place on a baking sheet and repeat to make 12–16 falafel balls.

Spray the falafel balls with cooking spray. Bake on the bottom rack of the oven for 15 minutes. Turn the oven down to 350 degrees F and move the baking sheet to the top rack. Bake for an additional 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a small jar or bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, remaining garlic, and 1 tbsp chopped fresh dill. Shake or whisk until emulsified. Season with 1/8 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp pepper.
To assemble, divide romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and ¼ cup fresh chopped parsley between bowls.
Drizzle with the lemon-herb vinaigrette and toss to coat. Top with warm falafel and serve immediately.

title: Sheet-Pan Cabbage Pizzas with "Sausage" Crumbles, Peppers, and Onions
description: This veggie-forward cabbage pizza swaps dough for roasted cabbage wedges, keeping carbohydrates low while packing in flavor, protein, and non-starchy vegetables. A blend of cottage cheese and reduced-fat mozzarella delivers creamy, melty goodness. Tofu "sausage" crumbles add savory plant-based protein, and roasted onions and bell peppers boost fiber and veggie content, making this a diabetes-friendly, vegetarian main dish that's hearty and satisfying. Finished with a tangy non-fat Greek yogurt ranch drizzle for a creamy, protein-rich topping.
serving_size: 2 cabbage rounds with toppings + 2 tbsp yogurt sauce
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 33g 12%; Dietary Fiber 11g 39%; Total Sugars 16g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 27g; Potassium 950mg 20%
ingredients: 1 large green cabbage (about 2 ½ lb, cut into 8 rounds about 3/8-inch-thick)
2 sprays, 0.50 g olive oil cooking spray
1 (14-oz) can canned whole tomatoes (no salt added)
14 oz extra firm tofu (pressed and crumbled)
1 tbsp lower sodium soy sauce (or tamari)
1 cup onion(s) (yellow or white, thinly sliced)
steps: In a medium bowl, hand-crush the tomatoes or pulse lightly in a blender until mostly smooth. Stir in the minced garlic, ½ teaspoon of the oregano, and ¼ teaspoon of the black pepper. Set aside.

Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line two large sheet pans with parchment paper. Arrange cabbage rounds in a single layer and lightly coat both sides with cooking spray. Scatter the bell peppers and onions around the cabbage. Roast for 20–25 minutes, flipping the cabbage halfway, until tender and lightly browned.

While the cabbage roasts, heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Add the crumbled tofu and cook for 2–3 minutes to drive off moisture. Add the soy sauce, fennel seed, garlic powder, remaining ½ tsp oregano, remaining ¼ tsp black pepper, and crushed red pepper flakes. Cook, stirring frequently, until lightly browned and aromatic, about 8–10 minutes.

Whisk together the non-fat Greek yogurt, lemon juice, dill, remaining 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and onion powder. Add water 1 tablespoon at a time until the drizzle reaches a pourable consistency. Set aside.

Remove cabbage rounds from the oven. Spoon 3 tablespoons of tomato sauce onto each round. Dollop 2 tablespoons of fat-free cottage cheese evenly over the sauce on each round, then sprinkle the pizzas evenly with the reduced fat mozzarella. Top with tofu crumbles, peppers, and onions. Return to the oven and bake for 10–15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and everything is heated through.
Let the pizzas cool for 5 minutes then scatter basil leaves over the top. Drizzle the yogurt ranch over each pizza just before serving. Serve 2 cabbage pizza rounds per person.

title: Turkey and Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms
description: Turn your appetizer game up a notch with our Turkey and Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms—a savory symphony that transforms ordinary cremini mushrooms into bite-sized wonders. These little powerhouses feature cremini mushrooms cradling a lively mix of fresh spinach, lean ground turkey, and a touch of Parmesan, ensuring a diabetes-friendly twist on a classic.
nutrients_raw: Calories 50; Total Fat 1g 1%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 15mg 5%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 8g; Potassium 217mg 5%
ingredients: 16 large cremini (baby bella) mushrooms (cleaned and stems removed)
steps: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F and prepare a baking sheet by lining it with parchment paper or lightly greasing it with cooking spray.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook the lean ground turkey, breaking it into small pieces, until it's browned and fully cooked. Drain any excess fat.
In the same skillet, add finely diced onion and minced garlic, and sauté for 2–3 minutes until they become fragrant and slightly softened.
Add the chopped fresh spinach to the skillet and cook for another 2–3 minutes until it wilts and any excess moisture evaporates.
Stir in the grated Parmesan cheese, dried oregano and rosemary. Season the mixture with salt and pepper. Mix well and let it cool slightly.
Take the cleaned mushrooms and lightly brush or spray them with cooking spray or olive oil. Arrange them on the prepared baking sheet with the gill side up.
Fill each mushroom cap with the turkey and spinach mixture, pressing it down slightly to pack it in.
Bake the stuffed mushrooms in the preheated oven for about 15–20 minutes or until the mushrooms are tender, and the filling is heated through and slightly browned.
Remove the stuffed mushrooms from the oven and allow them to cool for a few minutes before serving.

title: Honey and Cinnamon Roasted Almonds
description: Satisfy your craving for sweet and crunchy with these Honey and Cinnamon Roasted Almonds. Perfectly suited for any occasion, these roasted almonds redefine the snack game with a health-conscious twist, proving that delicious and diabetes-friendly can indeed go hand in hand.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 15g 19%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 6g; Potassium 140mg 3%
steps: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F and cover a sheet pan in parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, toss almonds with ground cinnamon, salt and honey.
Spread the almonds on a sheet pan and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally until golden brown.
Allow the almonds to cool. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.

title: Spiced Sesame Peanuts
description: Sweet, spicy, and crunchy? Check, check, check! These Spiced Sesame Peanuts are bathed in the richness of maple syrup, embrace the warmth of cinnamon, and get a kick from a subtle cayenne pepper zing. It's not just a snack—it's a flavor expedition that caters to your cravings while keeping things mindful.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 105mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 7g; Potassium 161mg 3%
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F and cover a sheet pan with parchment paper. In a small saucepan over medium high heat, whisk together maple syrup, salt, cinnamon, and cayenne.
Bring to a boil and remove from heat immediately.
Fold the peanuts and sesame seeds into the maple syrup mixture and spread evenly on the sheet pan.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until golden brown.
Remove the sheet pan from the oven and allow the peanuts to cool.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature.

title: Crispy Buffalo Chickpeas
description: Spice up your snacking routine with our Crispy Buffalo Chickpeas, where humble chickpeas undergo a fiery transformation. They make a great snack at home or your next tailgating party for a side that’s diabetes friendly and delicious.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 19g 7%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 215mg 5%
ingredients: 2 cans (15 ounces each) canned chickpeas (drained and rinsed)
1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (adjust to your preference)
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F and prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper or a light coating of cooking spray (optional).
Drain and rinse two cans of chickpeas, then gently pat them dry with a paper towel to remove excess moisture. Dry chickpeas will become crispier during roasting.
In a mixing bowl, toss the dried chickpeas with one tablespoon of olive oil, ensuring they are evenly coated.

In another bowl, create a spicy seasoning mixture by combining 1/4 cup of hot sauce, 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon of onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon of paprika, 1/2 teaspoon of cayenne pepper (adjust to your spice preference), and pepper.
Add the seasoned hot sauce mixture to the chickpeas, ensuring they are well-coated with the flavorful seasoning.
Spread the seasoned chickpeas onto the prepared baking sheet, ensuring they are in a single layer.
Bake the chickpeas in the preheated oven for about 55 minutes, or until they become crispy. Be sure to stir or shake the pan every 10-15 minutes for even cooking.
Once the chickpeas are crispy and have absorbed the Buffalo flavor, remove them from the oven and allow them to cool slightly.

title: Smoky Black Bean Dip
description: Dive into flavor paradise with our Smoky Black Bean Dip, a zesty sensation that transforms ordinary black beans into a smoky fiesta. Serve this dip with some fresh veggies for a healthy, low-carb snack or appetizer that’s perfect for people with and without diabetes.
serving_size: 1/4 cup dip + 1/2 cup sliced cucumber and bell pepper
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 430mg 9%
ingredients: 1 can (15 ounces) black beans (No added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: Use a food processor to combine the drained and rinsed black beans, minced garlic, chopped fresh cilantro, lime juice, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Blend until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. You can gradually drizzle in 1 tablespoon of olive oil while blending to create your desired texture. Feel free to adjust the amount of oil according to your preference.
After blending, taste the dip and make any necessary adjustments to the seasonings. You can add more salt, pepper, or lime juice to suit your taste.
Transfer the black bean dip to a serving bowl and gently swirl in 2 tablespoons of plain Greek yogurt. This addition provides a creamy element and a touch of tanginess to the dip.
Serve with sliced cucumbers and bell peppers.

title: Pan-Roasted Padron Peppers with Salt
description: Pan-roasted Padron peppers with salt is a simple and delightful dish that highlights the unique flavor of Padron peppers. These small green peppers are known for their mild, slightly sweet flavor, with the occasional spicy kick.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 193mg 4%
steps: Heat a large, heavy skillet or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add 1–2 tablespoons of olive oil, depending on your preference and the size of your skillet.

When the oil is hot and shimmering, add the Padron peppers to the skillet. You can leave them whole with the stems on. Let the peppers cook, undisturbed, for about 3–5 minutes or until they start to blister and char. Use tongs to turn them occasionally, so they cook evenly.
Once the Padron peppers are tender, blistered, and slightly charred, remove them from the skillet and transfer to a serving plate.
While the peppers are still hot, generously sprinkle them with coarse sea salt.

title: Tuna Avocado Spread
description: This Tuna Avocado Spread is a delightful fusion of omega-3-rich tuna and creamy avocado goodness. Whether you’re topping crackers, spreading it on toast, or dipping veggies, this tuna and avocado duo is a delicious and diabetes-friendly way to indulge in a spread that’s both wholesome and indulgent.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 15mg 5%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 6g 2%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 10g; Potassium 390mg 8%
ingredients: 1 can (5 ounces) tuna packed in water (drained)
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the drained tuna, mashed ripe avocado, plain Greek yogurt, fresh lemon juice, finely chopped green onions, finely diced celery, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir the ingredients until well combined, ensuring the tuna and avocado are evenly distributed and the mixture has a creamy consistency.
Taste the spread and adjust the seasonings, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed to suit your taste.

title: Winter Crudité with Herb Aioli
description: Winter Crudité with Herb Aioli is a refreshing and vibrant appetizer that features a selection of seasonal vegetables served with a flavorful herb-infused aioli. This recipe is a perfect addition to winter gatherings and holiday parties.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 470mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 3g; Potassium 471mg 10%
ingredients: 4 cup assorted vegetables (such as carrots, radishes, celery, broccoli, cauliflower, cherry tomatoes, and bell pepper strips)
2 tbsp fresh herbs (such as rosemary, chives, and parsley; finely chopped)
steps: Start by washing and preparing a variety of winter non-starchy vegetables like carrots, radishes, celery, broccoli, cauliflower, cherry tomatoes, and bell pepper strips. Cut them into bite-sized sticks or florets for easy dipping.

Once the vegetables are ready, arrange them beautifully on a serving platter, creating an inviting display. To enhance their flavors, lightly drizzle a small amount of olive oil over the vegetables and season them with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Take a small bowl and combine 1/2 cup of mayonnaise with fresh lemon juice, maple syrup, grated garlic, salt and pepper and finely chopped fresh herbs, such as rosemary, chives, and parsley. Stir the mixture until the herbs are evenly distributed throughout the aioli. Season the herb aioli with salt and pepper, adjusting the herbs to your preference.

title: Cauliflower "Popcorn"
description: Crispy and crunchy, this unique take on popcorn is a delicious, low-carb snack!
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 628mg 13%
ingredients: 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (adjust to your spice preference)
steps: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees F and prepare a baking sheet by lining it with parchment paper or lightly greasing it with cooking spray.
Take a head of cauliflower and cut it into small florets. In a large mixing bowl, toss these cauliflower florets with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, making sure they are evenly coated.

In a separate bowl, mix together 1/2 teaspoon of garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon of onion powder, 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika, ½ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon black pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon of cayenne pepper (adjust according to your spice preference).
Sprinkle this spice mixture over the cauliflower and toss to ensure the florets are well coated with these flavorful seasonings.
Spread the seasoned cauliflower in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake the cauliflower in the preheated oven for around 20–25 minutes, or until the florets become tender and slightly crispy. Be sure to stir or shake the pan occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Once the "popcorn” reaches your desired level of crispiness, remove it from the oven.

title: Spinach and Feta Stuffed Mushrooms
description: Spinach and Feta Stuffed Mushrooms are a delightful and savory appetizer that brings together the earthy flavor of mushrooms with a creamy and flavorful filling. These savory bites make an excellent appetizer for parties, holiday gatherings, or as a delicious addition to a tapas spread.
nutrients_raw: Calories 70; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 190mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 139mg 3%
ingredients: 16 large cremini (baby bella) mushrooms (cleaned and stems removed)
steps: Preheat your oven to 375 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and chopped spinach, and sauté for 2–3 minutes until the spinach wilts and any excess moisture evaporates. Remove the skillet from the heat.
In a mixing bowl, combine the sautéed spinach and garlic with crumbled feta cheese, grated Parmesan cheese, plain Greek yogurt, salt, and pepper. Ensure all the ingredients are thoroughly mixed.
Take the cleaned mushrooms and fill each cap with the spinach and cheese mixture, gently pressing it down.
Arrange the stuffed mushrooms on the prepared baking sheet. If desired, you can lightly spray them with cooking spray to aid in browning.
Bake the stuffed mushrooms in the preheated oven for approximately 15–20 minutes or until they become tender, and the filling is heated through and slightly browned.

title: Baked Chai Apple Chips
description: Baked apple chips are a delicious crunchy and sweet treat. This recipe adds chai flavoring, a warming blend of spices that’s perfect for a healthy fall and winter weather snack.
nutrients_raw: Calories 40; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 0g; Potassium 85mg 2%
ingredients: 2 med apple (sweet varieties like Fuji or Honeycrisp)
steps: Preheat your oven to 200 degrees F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. You can also lightly grease the parchment paper with cooking spray to prevent sticking.

Wash and core the apples, removing the seeds and stems. You can leave the peel on for added texture and nutrients. Using a mandoline slicer or a sharp knife, thinly slice the apples into rounds, aiming for slices of about 1/8-inch thickness. Make sure they are consistently thin for even baking.
In a small bowl, mix the ground cinnamon, ground cardamom, ground ginger, ground cloves, and ground nutmeg to create a chai spice blend.

Lay out the apple slices on the prepared baking sheets in a single layer, ensuring they do not overlap. Sprinkle the chai spice blend evenly over the apple slices. You can use your fingers or a shaker to distribute the spices evenly.

Place the baking sheets in the preheated oven and bake for about 2 hours. You'll want to check the apple chips occasionally to prevent overcooking. The chips are done when they become crisp but not burnt. They will become even crispier as they cool.

title: Tomato and Zucchini Salsa
description: This tomato and zucchini salsa is a versatile and nutritious option that celebrates the flavors of fresh, seasonal produce. Enjoy its crisp texture and vibrant taste as a delightful addition to your meals or as a standalone snack.
nutrients_raw: Calories 25; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 6g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 248mg 5%
ingredients: 1 small jalapeño pepper (seeded and finely minced)
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the diced tomatoes, diced zucchini, finely chopped red onion, chopped cilantro, and minced jalapeño pepper. Add the minced garlic to the mixture. Drizzle the fresh lime juice over the ingredients. Season the salsa with salt and pepper.
Gently toss all the ingredients together until they are well mixed and coated with the lime juice and seasonings.
Let the salsa sit for about 10–15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together. Adjust the seasoning to suit your preference

title: Almond Butter Toast with Fresh Pear
description: Enjoy a sweet and savory start to your day. This Almond Butter Toast with Fresh Pears is a harmonious blend of nutty almonds and bright peaches, plush a dash of spicy cinnamon. Enjoy another take on this breakfast in the summer when flavorful, ripe peaches are in season.
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 8g; Potassium 264mg 6%
steps: Toast the bread and spread almond butter.
Top with sliced pears and sprinkle with cinnamon.

title: Tomato and Basil Omelet
description: Start your day off with a savory Tomato and Basil Omelet. Incorporating egg whites helps lower the saturated fat while fresh tomato and basil add in a punch of color and flavor.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 430mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 14g; Potassium 404mg 9%
steps: Whisk the eggs in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour the beaten eggs into the pan.
Sprinkle diced tomato and chopped basil on half the omelet.
Once the eggs are set, fold the omelet in half and cook until the tomato softens, about 30 seconds.

title: Cinnamon Apple Oatmeal
description: Fresh apples make this oatmeal a perfect fall breakfast. A sprinkle of spices adds a depth of flavor to this diabetes-friendly Cinnamon Apple Oatmeal that the whole family will love.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 213mg 5%
steps: In a saucepan, bring water to a boil.
Stir in oats and reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes or until oats begin to thicken.
Add milk, diced apple, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the oats are creamy, and the apples are tender (about 5 more minutes).
Remove from heat and let it sit for a minute to thicken.
Divide the oatmeal into two bowls. Serve warm.

title: Spinach and Feta Omelet
description: Green fresh spinach, crunchy onions, and a touch of creamy feta cheese make this omelet one you’ll want to make again and again.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 440mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 16g; Potassium 588mg 13%
steps: In a bowl, season the egg substitute with salt and pepper and mix together.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add diced red onions and sauté until softened.
Add chopped spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted.
Pour the whisked eggs over the spinach and onions.
As the eggs begin to set, sprinkle diced tomatoes and crumbled feta cheese over half the omelet.
Once the eggs are fully set, carefully fold the omelet in half with a spatula.
Slide the omelet onto a plate, garnish with fresh herbs if desired, and serve.

title: Mexican-Inspired Breakfast Bowl
description: Zesty with a hint of spice, this Mexican-Inspired Breakfast Bowl ​is a delight​​ ​for the tastebuds. With fresh veggies and cauliflower rice, it’s a low carb way to start your day.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 10g; Potassium 335mg 7%
ingredients: 1 whole lime (cut into wedges, for serving)
steps: In a skillet, heat oil over medium heat.
Add diced onions and cook until softened.
Stir in cauliflower rice and cook for 3–5 minutes until it begins to soften.
Add diced bell peppers, black beans, ground cumin, and chili powder to the skillet. Cook for an additional 3–5 minutes. Season the mixture with salt and pepper.
Push the mixture to the side of the skillet, creating wells for the eggs.
Crack one egg into each well and cook until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny. If desired, cover the skillet to help the eggs cook more evenly.
Once the eggs are cooked to your liking, remove the skillet from heat.
Divide the egg, cauliflower rice and veggie mixture into four bowls.
Top each bowl with salsa and fresh cilantro, if using. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Salmon, Avocado, and Chickpea Breakfast Bowl
description: Want a protein rich breakfast? Try this diabetes-friendly Salmon and Avocado Bowl! It’s a healthy way to start your day.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 15g 19%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 15mg 5%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 14g 5%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 15g; Potassium 490mg 10%
ingredients: 1 cup canned chickpeas (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a bowl, toss the mixed salad greens with olive oil, lemon juice, and pepper.
Divide the dressed salad greens into 4 bowls.
Arrange smoked salmon slices, ​​avocado slices​, and chickpeas​ on top of the salad greens.​ ​
Garnish with capers and fresh dill​.​​

title: Banana and Almond Butter Toast
description: Almond butter and bananas are a perfect pairing for this diabetes-friendly breakfast toast. Filling and satisfying, you’ll feel powered to start your morning off right.
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 170mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 7g; Potassium 320mg 7%
steps: Toast the bread slice to your liking.
Spread almond butter evenly over the toasted bread.
Arrange banana slices on top of the almond butter.
Sprinkle sliced almonds over the banana slices.

title: Ham and Broccoli Breakfast Casserole
description: Casseroles are a great option to feed a crowd without a lot of work. This Ham and Broccoli Breakfast Casserole can be made the night before and popped in the over for an easy start to breakfast.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 20mg 7%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 15g; Potassium 286mg 6%
steps: Grease a 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray.
Spread diced ham and blanched broccoli evenly in the baking dish.
In a bowl, whisk together egg substitute, milk, Dijon mustard, garlic powder, and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the ham and broccoli in the baking dish.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar and grated Parmesan cheese over the top.
Cover the baking dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight (if desired)
When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Remove the casserole from the refrigerator and let it come to room temperature while the oven preheats.
Bake for 40–45 minutes or until the center is set and the top is golden brown.
Allow the casserole to cool for a few minutes before slicing.

title: Spinach and Mozzarella Egg White Bites
description: It’s easy to make your own egg bites at home! That way, you can monitor exactly what goes into them. These low carb Spinach and ​Mozzarella​​ Egg White Bites make for a quick grab-and-go breakfast you can meal prep ahead of time.
nutrients_raw: Calories 70; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 2g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 110mg 2%
ingredients: 1 cup egg whites (about 8 large egg whites)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced red onions and cook until softened.
Add chopped spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted.
In a bowl, whisk the egg whites and season with oregano, salt, and pepper.
Grease a muffin tin with cooking spray.
Distribute the sautéed spinach and onions evenly among the muffin tin cups.
Pour the whisked egg whites over the spinach and onions in each cup. Sprinkle diced tomatoes and mozzarella cheese on top.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes or until the egg whites are set.
Allow the egg white bites to cool for a few minutes before removing them from the muffin tin.

title: Carrot "Cake" Muffins
description: If you love carrot cake, then you’ll love these Carrot “Cake” Muffins! Low carb and diabetes-friendly, these muffins are sure to be enjoyed by the whole family.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 15g 19%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 120mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 133mg 3%
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a muffin tin with paper liners.
In a large bowl, combine almond flour, all-purpose flour, shredded carrots, chopped ​walnuts, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
In another bowl, whisk together eggs, applesauce, ​olive oil, almond milk, sugar substitute, and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Spoon the batter evenly into the muffin cups, filling each about 2/3 full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 18–20 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

title: Vegetable Breakfast Hash
description: This Vegetable Breakfast Hash is a hearty way to start your day and works great for brunch! You can customize this hash by swapping in any of your favorite non-starchy veggies.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 9g; Potassium 668mg 14%
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onions and potatoes and cook until the onions are softened.
Stir in diced bell pepper and zucchini and season with black pepper and ¼ teaspoon salt. Cook for 5–7 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Add cherry tomatoes, minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, ¼ teaspoon salt, and pepper. Cook for an additional 3–5 minutes, allowing tomatoes to soften.
Create four wells in the vegetable mixture.
Crack one egg into each well. Season with ¼ teaspoon salt and black pepper.
Cover the skillet and cook for 5–7 minutes or until the eggs are cooked to your liking.

title: Chickpea Shakshuka
description: Chickpea Shakshuka is a delightful and nutritious twist on the classic shakshuka. For some extra plant-based protein, chickpeas are added to this flavor-packed breakfast.
nutrients_raw: Calories 260; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 440mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 29g 11%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 13g; Potassium 400mg 9%
ingredients: 1 (14 ounce) can canned diced tomatoes (no salt added)
1 (14 ounce) can canned chickpeas (low sodium, drained and rinsed)
1 small whole wheat pita (cut into fourths)
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for an additional 30 seconds.
Sprinkle ground cumin, paprika, and ground coriander over the onions and garlic.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chickpeas. Season with ½ teaspoon each salt and pepper. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the mixture thickens.
Make small wells in the mixture and crack the eggs into each well. Spring with ½ teaspoon salt.
Cover the skillet and cook for 5–7 minutes, or until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still runny (adjust cooking time based on egg preference).
Garnish with chopped fresh basil and serve with slice of pita.

title: Poached Eggs with Sautéed Greens
description: This colorful breakfast is a healthy way to start your day! Mixed greens provide fiber and nutrients for a diabetes-friendly meal that you’ll feel good about eating.
nutrients_raw: Calories 290; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 31g 11%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 15g; Potassium 451mg 10%
ingredients: 4 cup mixed greens (such as spinach, kale, Swiss chard; chopped)
2 slice whole grain bread (toasted, cut in half)
steps: Fill a wide, shallow pan with water and bring it to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar to the water.
Crack each egg into a small bowl.
Carefully slide each egg into the simmering water, one at a time. Poach for 3–4 minutes for a runny yolk, or longer for a firmer yolk.
While the eggs are poaching, heat oil in a separate skillet over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for an additional 30 seconds.
Add the chopped mixed greens to the skillet and sauté until wilted.
Season the greens with​ salt and ​pepper.
Remove the poached eggs from the water using a slotted spoon and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess water.
Serve the poached eggs on a bed of sautéed greens with whole-grain bread on the side.

title: Apple Cinnamon Quinoa Porridge
description: Enjoy the flavors of fall in this hearty Apple Cinnamon Quinoa Porridge. Filled with fiber, it’s a healthy way to start your day!
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 320mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 13g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 4g; Potassium 294mg 6%
steps: In a medium-sized saucepan, combine quinoa, almond milk, diced apples, maple syrup, ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, and salt.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15–20 minutes or until the quinoa is cooked and the porridge has thickened.
Stir the porridge occasionally during cooking to prevent sticking.
Once cooked, remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for an additional 5 minutes.
Fluff the quinoa with a fork and adjust sweetness if necessary.
Serve the porridge in bowls, topped with chopped nuts if desired.

title: Green Goddess Turkey Burger
description: A Green Goddess Turkey Burger is a tasty and healthy alternative to traditional beef burgers, featuring ground turkey and a vibrant green goddess sauce made with fresh herbs. Add some fresh avocado, tomato, or sliced onion to your burger for some additional flavor and texture.
nutrients_raw: Calories 370; Total Fat 15g 19%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 33g; Potassium 567mg 12%
ingredients: 1/4 cup Plain Nonfat Greek yogurt (for dressing)
1/3 cup green onion (scallion) (cut into 1-inch pieces, for dressing)
1/2 tbsp chopped, 1 tbsp minced garlic (divided use)
steps: Put the ingredients for the Green Goddess sauce into a food processor and blend until smooth. Transfer to a bowl.
In a medium bowl, add the ground turkey, onion, 1 tbsp minced garlic, almond meal or almond flour, Dijon mustard, paprika, kosher salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Divide the meat into four equal parts and form them into 1/2-inch-thick patties that are slightly wider than the buns.
In a large frying pan on medium heat, add the olive oil. When the oil shimmers, add the four burgers, leaving space between them.
Cook the patties for 3–4 minutes. Flip them and cook for another 3–4 minutes, or until their internal temperature registers 165 degrees F.
Spread green goddess sauce on the top and bottom of a toasted bun. Layer the bottom bun with a patty and lettuce and enjoy.

title: Magic Air Fried Chicken Nuggets with Sweet and Sour Sauce
description: What’s magic about these chicken nuggets? The fact that they’re so delicious and diabetes friendly, plus kid approved!
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 90mg 30%; Sodium 450mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 12g; Potassium 190mg 4%
ingredients: 2 whole boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cubed into nugget-sized pieces)
steps: In a small saucepan, combine honey, ketchup, apple cider vinegar, and soy sauce. Heat the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly until well combined and slightly thickened. Remove from heat and set aside.
Mix the chicken with kosher salt, pepper, and lemon juice. You can leave it for 30 minutes to 1 to 2 hours for flavors to develop, although it's not necessary.
Put the flour in a shallow bowl.
Lightly whisk eggs in a separate bowl.
Put crushed cornflakes in another shallow bowl.
Preheat your air fryer to 375 degrees F.
Dip each chicken nugget first into the flour, then into the egg, and finally into the cornflakes mix. Make sure to coat each nugget thoroughly by pressing the cornflakes onto them.
Place the coated chicken nuggets in the air fryer basket in a single layer. Spray oil on the nuggets liberally, covering all surfaces.
Cook at 375 degrees F for 10 to 12 minutes, or until the nuggets are golden and crispy with an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, flipping them over halfway through the cooking time.
Serve the air-fried chicken nuggets with the homemade sweet and sour sauce for dipping.

title: Air Fryer Smoky Herb Chicken Tenders
description: Take your chicken dinner to the next level with this smoky, herby chicken tender recipe. Air frying chicken keeps them moist and delicious, plus makes it a quick and easy dinner to make.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 125mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 26g; Potassium 414mg 9%
ingredients: 1 lbs chicken tenderloins (boneless, skinless, cut in half)
steps: Preheat the air fryer to 400 degrees F, or an oven to 420 degrees F
Combine paprika, cumin, dried oregano, and cayenne pepper in a small bowl.
Lightly spray the tenders with oil, then rub the spice mixture all over the chicken. For best results, let it marinate for at least 20 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Add the chicken to an air fryer basket or a baking tray (lined with parchment or foil).
Air fry for 12–15 minutes or bake for 16–20 minutes until the chicken is 165 degrees F internally.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajita Bowl
description: Sheet pan dinners are a great option for a quick and easy weeknight meal without a lot of clean up. This Mexican-inspired sheet pan chicken fajitas make a filling and delicious bowl.
serving_size: 6 ounces chicken + 1 cup vegetable bean mixture
nutrients_raw: Calories 380; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 95mg 32%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 9g 32%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 43g; Potassium 1166mg 25%
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into 1 inch slices)
1 (15 ounce) can black beans (low sodium, drained and rinsed)
steps: Heat the oven to 425 degrees F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

In a large bowl, combine chili powder, cumin, kosher salt, garlic powder, paprika, and ground pepper. Whisk in 1 tablespoon of oil. Add the chicken, onion, and red and green bell peppers and toss to coat.
Spread the chicken and vegetables in a single layer on the sheet pan. Bake for 15 minutes.
Combine black beans and the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large bowl.
Remove the pan from the oven and stir the chicken and vegetables. Spread beans evenly over the top. Roast until the chicken is 165 degrees F and the vegetables are tender, 5–7 minutes more.
In a small bowl, stir yogurt, lime juice, and hot sauce.
Divide the lettuce, chicken, beans, and vegetables among the four bowls. Drizzle with the yogurt sauce and serve with additional hot sauce or salsa.

title: Coconut Almond Chicken Tenders with Sweet Spicy Sauce
description: Sweet coconut and almond pair perfectly with a spicy sauce to take these chicken tenders to the next level.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 35mg 12%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 17g 6%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 19g; Potassium 252mg 5%
ingredients: 2 whole boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into 8-1 inch strips)
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and cover a sheet pan with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs to break them up.
In another medium bowl, whisk together the panko, shredded coconut, chopped almonds, and garlic powder.
Dip each chicken strip first in egg and then in coconut mixture, making sure to coat it well with the crumbs.
Place on the baking sheet and bake until the tenders have an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 15 minutes.
For the dipping sauce, whisk together apricot jam, garlic chili sauce and kosher salt. Thin with 1-2 tablespoons of water and strain, if desired.
Serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Chicken Tikka Kebabs
description: These Chicken Tika Kebabs are a diabetes-friendly way to enjoy perfectly spiced Indian food without a lot of calories or carbs.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 6g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 29g; Potassium 572mg 12%
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into 1-inch cubes)
1 large red bell pepper (cut into 1-inch pieces)
steps: In a large bowl stir the garlic, yogurt, lemon zest and juice, spices, and kosher salt until combined.
Add the chicken to the bowl and stir until all the cubes are evenly coated in the marinade. Cover and allow to marinate for 20 minutes (or place in the fridge for up to 24 hours).
Discard the marinade and thread the chicken onto the skewers, alternating with the bell pepper and onion.

Lightly grease the grill, grill pan, or griddle and place on high heat. Once hot, place the skewers on the grill, rotating to ensure even cooking, for 12–15 minutes depending on the thickness of your chicken.
Allow the kebabs to rest, covered, for 5 minutes before serving with tzatziki sauce

title: Chicken Fried Cauliflower Rice
description: This Cauliflower Chicken Fried Rice is a great low-carb option when you’re craving Asian food. Using cauliflower rice and fresh veggies, it’s a colorful and nutritious dinner that is easy to throw together.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 75mg 25%; Sodium 450mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 18g; Potassium 692mg 15%
ingredients: 1 cup mixed vegetables (such as peas, carrots, corn, bell peppers; chopped)
1 cup boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cooked, diced)
steps: In a large nonstick skillet or wok, heat 1 tablespoon oil over medium-high heat.
Add minced ginger and garlic, sautéing for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetables, cauliflower rice, soy sauce and sesame oil to the skillet and stir-fry for 7-8 minutes, until cooked through and browned in parts.
Stir the diced chicken into the skillet.

Push the mixture to the side of the skillet and add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in the empty space. Pour the beaten eggs into the empty space. Scramble the eggs until just barely cooked. Mix the eggs into the vegetable and chicken mixture.
Finish with the green onions.

title: Sautéed Chicken Sausage and Peppers
description: Sautéed Chicken Sausage and Peppers, a quick and flavorful dish that brings together the savory taste of chicken sausage with sweet and colorful bell peppers. This diabetes-friendly version is full of veggies, making it a healthy and satisfying meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 250; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 25mg 8%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 1251mg 27%
ingredients: 1 lbs chicken sausage links (low sodium, sliced)
steps: Bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add cubed potato and cook for 7 minutes. Drain.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced chicken sausage to the skillet and sauté until browned on all sides, approximately 5-7 minutes.
Remove the sausage from the skillet and set aside. Add the sliced onions and peppers to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 10 minutes.
Season the mixture with minced garlic, dried oregano, dried basil, fresh thyme, kosher salt, and pepper. Stir well to combine.
Add the potatoes and sausage back to the skillet and sauté 2-3 minutes more. Serve warm.

title: Spice Rubbed Pork Tenderloin
description: This spice-rubbed pork tenderloin is flavorful, juicy, and has a perfect balance of sweet, savory, and spicy notes. It's a versatile dish that pairs well with various sides, such as roasted vegetables or a fresh salad.
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 100mg 33%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 2g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 32g; Potassium 641mg 14%
steps: In a small bowl, mix together the cumin, smoked paprika, minced garlic, onion powder, dried oregano, brown sugar, kosher salt, and black pepper to create the spice rub.
Pat the pork tenderloins dry with paper towels.
Rub the spice mixture evenly over the surface of each pork tenderloin, ensuring they are well coated.
Let the pork rest for 30 minutes. For a more intense flavor, you can cover and refrigerate the pork for up to 4 hours.
Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the pork tenderloins on all sides until deeply browned, about 5 minutes per side.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and roast for approximately 10–15 minutes or until the internal temperature reaches 145 degrees F.
Remove the pork from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Slice into medallions and serve.

title: Besan Chilla
description: Made with chickpea flour and colorful vegetables, besan chilla is a popular savory pancake enjoyed in many Indian households. Its lightly nutty flavor, crisp edges, and tender center make it a tasty snack or light meal, while the chickpea flour provides protein and fiber.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 520mg 11%
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the besan, water, and spices until smooth.
Stir in the vegetables. Cover and set aside for 5-10 minutes. Mix well again.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat and lightly coat with cooking spray.
Pour the batter into the skillet, gently spread the batter evenly, and round off the shape to create a thin, 6-inch pancake.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until lightly browned and cooked through.
Serve warm with 1 Tbsp plain Greek yogurt on the side for dipping.

title: Peanut Chaat
description: Chaat is a beloved category of Indian street foods known for its bold flavors and exciting mix of textures. This version combines crunchy peanuts with crisp vegetables, fresh herbs, and a squeeze of lemon for a refreshing snack that’s rich in protein, healthy fats, and fiber.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 15g 19%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 13g 5%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 9g; Potassium 420mg 9%
ingredients: 1/2 small green chili (finely chopped, to taste)
steps: Combine all ingredients in a bowl. Toss gently and serve immediately.

title: Spinach and Ricotta Cheese Stuffed Chicken Breast
description: Stuffed chicken breasts are an easy way to enjoy lean protein while making it a fun dish with flair. This spinach and ricotta cheese version is diabetes-friendly and would pair great with non-starchy veggies like broccoli or asparagus.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 80mg 27%; Sodium 340mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars -0.01g <1%; Protein 29g; Potassium 410mg 9%
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F.
In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped baby spinach to the skillet and cook until wilted. Season with kosher salt, black pepper, and dried oregano. Remove from heat and stir in ricotta cheese.
Butterfly each chicken breast by cutting a slit horizontally through the center, leaving the edges intact.
Season the inside of each chicken breast with a pinch of kosher salt and black pepper.
Stuff each chicken breast with the spinach and ricotta cheese mixture.
Secure the edges of the chicken breasts with toothpicks to keep the stuffing in place.
Place the stuffed chicken breasts in a baking dish and bake in the preheated oven until the chicken has an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 25 minutes.

title: Baked BBQ Chicken Tenders
description: Baking chicken tenders is a healthy option that still is full of flavor. This BBQ version adds a fresh tang the whole family will enjoy.
