nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 95mg 32%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 6g 2%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 35g; Potassium 429mg 9%
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, whisk together tomato sauce, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, kosher salt, and black pepper.
Set aside half of the BBQ sauce for later use.
Place the chicken tenders in a resealable plastic bag or shallow dish.
Pour the other half of the BBQ sauce mixture over the chicken tenders. Seal the bag or cover the dish and let the chicken marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Arrange the chicken tenders on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through, flipping halfway through.
Serve with remaining BBQ sauce.

title: Sheet Pan Garlic Shrimp and Asparagus
description: Sheet pan dinners are quick and easy meals without a lot of clean up. This Garlic Shrimp and Asparagus version is ready to eat in 20 minutes!
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 160mg 53%; Sodium 310mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 22g; Potassium 279mg 6%
ingredients: 1 lbs shrimp (large, peeled and deveined, not packed in solution)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the shrimp and asparagus. Add olive oil, minced garlic, red pepper flakes (if using), kosher salt, and black pepper. Toss everything together until the shrimp and asparagus are evenly coated.
Spread the shrimp and asparagus in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for approximately 8–10 minutes or until the shrimp are opaque and the asparagus is tender but still crisp.

title: Turkey Meatballs and Zucchini Noodles
description: This Italian-inspired version features delicious turkey meatballs and low-carb zucchini noodles for a healthy meal the whole family will enjoy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 360; Total Fat 13g 17%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 100mg 33%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 12g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 35g; Potassium 1126mg 24%
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line two sheet pans with parchment paper.
In a mixing bowl, combine ground turkey, breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, egg, minced garlic, dried oregano, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper. Mix until well combined.
With wet hands, form the mixture into meatballs, approximately 1 inch in diameter, and place them on the sheet pan. Bake for 20 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees F.
While the meatballs bake, toss the zucchini noodles with olive oil, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper and spread them on the second sheet pan.
Bake until tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Warm marinara sauce on the stove and toss the warm meatballs in the sauce.
Serve meatballs over the zucchini noodles and garnish with the olives and fresh parsley.

title: Sheet Pan Balsamic Chicken and Brussels Sprouts
description: Sheet pan dinners are quick and easy meals without a lot of clean up. Elevate your chicken with delicious balsamic vinegar and a side of crispy brussels sprouts for the perfect and healthy weeknight dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 330; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 95mg 32%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 38g; Potassium 778mg 17%
ingredients: 4 whole boneless, skinless chicken breasts (6 ounces each)
1 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish, optional)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, olive oil, honey, minced garlic, dried thyme, kosher salt, and black pepper to create the marinade.
Place chicken breasts in a large bowl and pour the marinade over the chicken, ensuring it's well coated.
Arrange the chicken breasts on the sheet pan and Brussels sprouts on the other.
Add the Brussels sprouts to the same bowl and coat well with the remaining marinade. Arrange the Brussel sprouts around the chicken on the sheet pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until the chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 25–30 minutes.
Remove from the oven, let it rest for a few minutes, and then garnish with fresh parsley and lemon zest and juice, if using.

title: Homemade Chai
description: Chai is a cherished part of daily life in many Indian and South Asian homes, bringing together black tea, warming spices, and creamy milk in a comforting cup. This recipe has the naturally rich aroma and flavor of the tea and spices, making it easy to enjoy an authentic chai without added sugar.
nutrients_raw: Calories 50; Total Fat 1g 1%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 55mg 2%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 190mg 4%
steps: Bring water, ginger, cardamom, and cinnamon to a simmer.
Add the tea bag and steep for 3-5 minutes.
Stir in the milk and heat until warm.
Remove tea bag and strain out spices before serving.

title: Pesto Chicken
description: This Pesto Chicken recipe pairs nicely with zucchini noodles for a low-carb, Italian-inspired meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 80mg 27%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 29g; Potassium 267mg 6%
ingredients: 1 1/4 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (thinly sliced in half)
1 tbsp fresh basil (chopped, for garnish, optional)
steps: Preheat your grill or grill pan on medium-high heat. Brush with olive oil.
Place the chicken breasts in a shallow dish and coat them evenly with the pesto sauce.
Grill the marinated chicken breasts for about 6–8 minutes per side or until fully cooked, with an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.
Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes before serving.

title: Sheet Pan Herb Roasted Pork and Sweet Potatoes
description: Sheet pan dinners are quick and easy meals without a lot of clean up. This Herb Roasted Pork and Sweet Potatoes recipe is a classic, homecooked meal that you’ll want to add to your weekly rotation of dinner options.
serving_size: 4 ounces pork + 1/2 cup sweet potatoes and onions
nutrients_raw: Calories 280; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 23mg 8%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 24g; Potassium 603mg 13%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix together olive oil, minced garlic, dried rosemary, dried thyme, kosher salt, and black pepper.
Place pork tenderloin in the center of the prepared sheet pan. Brush with ½ of the herbed oil mixture.
Toss sweet potato chunks and red onion with the rest of the herbed oil. Scatter the vegetables around the pork on the sheet pan.
Roast until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees F, approximately 35–40 minutes, and the sweet potatoes are tender.
Remove from the oven and let the pork rest for a few minutes before slicing.
Serve the herb-roasted pork slices alongside the roasted sweet potatoes. Sprinkle chopped fresh parsley for garnish if desired.

title: Slow Cooker Braised Beef with Carrots and Turnips
description: Tender and moist, this Slow Cooker Braised Beef with Carrots and Turnips will be a hit with whoever eats it. Try serving this for your next Sunday family dinner!
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 60mg 20%; Sodium 330mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 13g 5%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 24g; Potassium 730mg 16%
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs beef roast, bottom round, lean, ⅛” trim, boneless (trimmed of fat)
steps: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Brown the beef chunks on all sides. Transfer the browned beef to the slow cooker.
In the same skillet, add the remaining tablespoon of oil if needed. Sauté the onions and garlic until softened.
Deglaze the skillet with water, scraping up any browned bits. Add tomato paste and stir to combine.
Transfer the onion and tomato mixture to the slow cooker.
Add carrots, turnips, dried thyme, bay leaves, salt and pepper to the slow cooker.
Pour the low sodium tomato sauce and the beef broth over the ingredients in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6–8 hours or until the beef is tender.
Before serving, discard bay leaves and adjust the seasoning if necessary.

title: Vegetable and Hummus Sandwich
description: This deliciously crunchy salad is a great healthy option for a no-cook lunch. Not only is it diabetes-friendly, it’s also vegan!
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 450mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 37g 13%; Dietary Fiber 9g 32%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 663mg 14%
steps: Lay out the slices of whole grain or whole wheat bread.
Spread a generous layer of hummus on each slice.
Divide the mixed salad greens evenly and place them on two slices of bread.
Top the greens with cucumber slices, bell pepper slices, tomato slices, red onion slices, and Kalamata olives.
Drizzle extra virgin olive oil over the vegetable layers. Season with black pepper.
Place the remaining slices of bread, hummus-side down, on top of the vegetables to form sandwiches. Press down gently to secure the layers.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Fajita Bowl
description: This delicious Chicken and Vegetable Fajita Bowl is a low carb way to enjoy Mexican inspired dishes. Add some fresh cilantro and lime wedges if you want to add a little something extra to this flavorful lunch recipe.
serving_size: about 1/2 cup chicken mixture + 1 cup cauliflower rice + 1/4 cup cherry tomatoes + 1/4 avocado
nutrients_raw: Calories 290; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 20g 7%; Dietary Fiber 8g 29%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 28g; Potassium 936mg 20%
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (sliced into strips)
steps: Mix spices in a small bowl and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine chicken strips, sliced bell peppers, sliced red onion, and seasoning blend.

Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Add olive oil and turn the pan to coat the bottom. Cook the seasoned chicken and vegetables until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender-crisp, about 5–7 minutes.
Divide cauliflower rice among four bowls. Top with the cooked chicken and vegetable mixture.
Add cherry tomatoes and sliced avocado to each bowl.

title: Smoked Salmon and Avocado Toast
description: Elevate your avocado toast game by adding some smoked salmon. Perfect for a quick and easy lunch, this diabetes-friendly recipe is a delicious one you’ll enjoy again and again.
nutrients_raw: Calories 220; Total Fat 13g 17%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 8g 29%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 12g; Potassium 488mg 10%
steps: Toast the slices of whole grain or whole wheat bread until golden brown.
While the bread is toasting, cut the avocado in half, remove the pit, and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Mash the avocado with a fork until smooth and spreadable.
Spread the mashed avocado evenly over the toasted bread.
Drape smoked salmon slices over the avocado.
Serve with lemon wedges and fresh parsley for garnish.

title: Broiled Tomato and Cheese Sandwich
description: If you love tomato soup with grilled cheese, then you’ll enjoy this diabetes-friendly Broiled Tomao and Cheese Toast!
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 13g; Potassium 219mg 5%
steps: Preheat the broiler in your oven.
Place the slices of whole grain or whole wheat bread on a baking sheet.
Lightly toast one side of the bread slices under the broiler for 1–2 minutes, keeping a close eye to prevent burning.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven and flip the bread slices to the untoasted side.
Spread a thin layer of basil pesto on each untoasted side of the bread.
Place tomato slices on the bread.
Top the tomatoes with slices of mozzarella cheese. Drizzle olive oil over the top.
Place the baking sheet back under the broiler for an additional 2–3 minutes or until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Top with sliced, fresh basil if desired.

title: Lemon Popsicles
description: Enjoy these Lemon Popsicles on a hot summer day. Fresh and citrusy, they are a refreshing, diabetes-friendly treat to cool down with.
nutrients_raw: Calories 10; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 0g; Potassium 36mg <1%
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, water, and stevia.
Pour into popsicle molds, using around 1/2 cup of liquid for each.
Freeze for 6 hours or overnight.

title: Honey, Vanilla, and Raspberry Yogurt Popsicles
description: These Honey, Vanilla and Raspberry Yogurt Popsicles are a creamy way to cool down. Diabetes-friendly, they are a kid-approved dessert that’s perfect in the summer.
nutrients_raw: Calories 70; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 20mg <1%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 7g; Potassium 142mg 3%
steps: In a blender, puree yogurt and raspberries.
Once blended, drizzle the honey and vanilla into the mix. Blend thoroughly.
Pour the mixture into popsicle molds. Freeze for 8 hours or overnight.

title: Honey and Walnut Stuffed Dates
description: Naturally sweet dates are the star of the show in these Honey and Walnut Stuffed Dates. Crunchy and earthy walnuts balance the flavor of a drizzle of honey for this dessert that’s a healthy option for people with diabetes.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 21g 8%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 19g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 1g; Potassium 160mg 3%
steps: Carefully cut a slit lengthwise in the pitted dates, gently open, and separate into halves.
Stuff each date half with a walnut half.
Drizzle honey over the stuffed dates before serving.

title: Baked Apples
description: Baked Apples are a delicious treat to make in the fall. Using the natural sweetness of apples, this recipe can be a diabetes-friendly dessert.
nutrients_raw: Calories 60; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 12g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 0g; Potassium 121mg 3%
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Cover a 9x9 inch baking dish with parchment paper.
Place apple slices in the prepared baking dish, drizzle with syrup, and sprinkle with cinnamon and nutmeg.
Stir to evenly coat the apples.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until the apples are tender. Serve warm.

title: Banana Popsicles
description: These Banana Popsicles are a sweet way to cool down. Diabetes-friendly and a kid-approved dessert that’s perfect in the summer.
nutrients_raw: Calories 70; Total Fat 1g 1%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 10mg <1%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 254mg 5%
steps: In a blender, combine the bananas, Greek yogurt, and syrup.
Pour the mixture into the popsicle molds and freeze for 8 hours or overnight.

title: Lemon Poppyseed Power Balls
description: Power-up your dessert with these delicious and nutritious Lemon Poppy Seed Power Balls. Made with hearty ingredients, these make an excellent dessert.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 60mg 3%; Total Carbohydrate 13g 5%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 93mg 2%
steps: Pulse the oats in the bowl of a food processor until they are finely ground.
Add the almonds and continue pulsing until it is a finely ground mixture.
Pour in the syrup along with the sunflower butter, lemon zest and juice, vanilla, and salt and blend until it turns into a dough.
Transfer the dough to a mixing bowl and stir in the poppy seeds.
Using a 2-tablespoon portion scoop, scoop out 20 balls. Roll each between your hands to form a smooth ball.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 12 days or in the freezer for 1 month.

title: Frozen Greek Yogurt Bark with Strawberries and Dark Chocolate
description: Frozen Greek Yogurt Bark with Strawberries and Dark Chocolate is a delicious frozen treat that combines the creaminess of Greek yogurt with the sweetness of strawberries and rich dark chocolate.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 25mg 1%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 7g; Potassium 167mg 4%
ingredients: 2 oz dark chocolate chips (no sugar added)
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine Greek yogurt, syrup, and vanilla extract. Mix until well combined.
Pour the Greek yogurt mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, spreading it into an even layer with a spatula.
Scatter sliced strawberries and chopped dark chocolate over the Greek yogurt.
Place the baking sheet in the freezer and let the yogurt bark freeze for at least 3 hours or until firm.
Once frozen, break the bark into pieces. Store in an airtight container in the freezer.

title: Apple Pear Crisp
description: Apple Pear Crisp is a warm and comforting dessert that combines the natural sweetness of apples and pears with a crunchy and spiced oat topping. This recipe is vegan and diabetes-friendly!
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 2g 3%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 55mg 2%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 122mg 3%
steps: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9 x 13 baking dish.

In a large bowl, combine the sliced apples, sliced pears, lemon juice, granulated sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. Toss until the fruits are well coated, and the sugar and spices are evenly distributed.
In a separate bowl, mix together oats, flour, brown sugar substitute, and diced cold plant-based butter. Use your hands or a pastry cutter to combine until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Spread the fruit mixture evenly in the prepared baking dish.
Sprinkle the oat and flour mixture over the top of the fruit, creating a crumbly topping.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes. Remove the foil and bake until the top is golden brown, and the fruit is bubbly, about 20 minutes more.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Banana Pineapple "Nice" Cream
description: Using bananas as the base ingredient, this “nice” cream recipe is a dairy-free and diabetes-friendly alternative to ice cream. Try topping it with some extra fresh fruit or nuts for an extra pop of flavor.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 0.5g <1%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 13g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 1g; Potassium 317mg 7%
steps: Place the banana slices and pineapple chunks in a single layer on a parchment-lined tray. Freeze for at least 2 hours or until solid.
In a high-powered blender or food processor, combine the frozen banana slices, frozen pineapple chunks, vanilla extract, and coconut milk.
Blend the ingredients until smooth and creamy, scraping down the sides as needed. If the mixture is too thick, you can add a bit more coconut milk to help with blending.
If you prefer a soft-serve texture, you can enjoy the "nice" cream immediately. If you prefer a firmer texture, transfer the mixture to an airtight container and freeze for an additional 1–2 hours.

title: Apple Squares
description: Apple Squares are a delicious dessert that is perfect anytime of the year. This kid-approved recipe is a family favorite and a great choice for people with diabetes.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 20mg 7%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 94mg 2%
ingredients: 1 cup white, whole wheat pastry flour
steps: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F. Line an 8 x 8-inch baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang for easy removal.
In a bowl, toss the diced apples with lemon juice to prevent browning. Set it aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, ground cinnamon, and salt.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the margarine, applesauce, granulated sugar substitute, brown sugar substitute, egg, and vanilla extract.
Gradually add the butter mixture to the flour mixture, stirring until just combined.
Gently fold in the diced apples and chopped walnuts.
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared baking pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 30 to 40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Allow to cool in the pan for 10 minutes before using the parchment paper overhang to lift them onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Once cooled, cut into 12 squares and serve.

title: Pumpkin Almond Smoothie
description: A Pumpkin Almond Smoothie is a delicious and nutritious beverage that captures the flavors of fall with pumpkin while adding the richness of almond.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 115mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 13g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 363mg 8%
ingredients: 1 cup canned pumpkin puree (no sugar added)
steps: In a blender, combine the canned pumpkin purée, sliced banana, almond milk, almond butter, ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, and vanilla extract.
Blend the ingredients on high speed until smooth and creamy.
If you prefer a colder smoothie, you can add a handful of ice cubes and blend again until well incorporated. Serve immediately.

title: Spiced Glazed Oranges
description: Spiced Honey Glazed Oranges is a simple and delightful diabetes-friendly dessert that combines the natural sweetness of oranges with a warm and aromatic honey-spice glaze. Top with fresh chopped mint leaves for an extra touch of color and flavor.
nutrients_raw: Calories 50; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 75mg 3%; Total Carbohydrate 13g 5%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 1g; Potassium 121mg 3%
ingredients: 2 large oranges (peeled and sliced into rounds)
steps: Peel the oranges and slice them into rounds. Remove any seeds.

In a small saucepan over low heat, combine honey, 1 tablespoons water, ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, ground ginger, and a pinch of sea salt. Stir until the mixture is well combined and heated through.
Arrange the orange slices on a serving platter or individual plates.
Drizzle the spiced honey glaze over the orange slices, ensuring each slice gets a flavorful coating.
Serve the oranges immediately.

title: Greek Yogurt Vanilla Mousse with Blueberries
description: Greek Yogurt Vanilla Mousse is a lighter alternative to traditional mousse, incorporating the tangy richness of Greek yogurt with the sweet and comforting flavors of vanilla. Add some fresh blueberries before serving for a beautiful dessert.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 15mg 5%; Sodium 75mg 3%; Total Carbohydrate 13g 5%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 8g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 13g; Potassium 240mg 5%
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the non-fat Greek yogurt, milk, heavy cream, maple syrup, and vanilla extract.
Use a hand mixer and beat until the mixture is well incorporated and fluffy.
Divide the Greek yogurt mixture into 4 serving cups or glasses.
Chill the mousse in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours to allow it to set.
Top each with ¼ cup fresh blueberries before serving.

title: Roasted Pears with Oat Crumble
description: This comforting dessert pairs roasted pears with a spiced oat topping. Naturally sweet and full of flavor, this diabetes-friendly treat is perfect for enjoying any time of year.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 176mg 4%
ingredients: 2 whole pears (ripe but firm, halved and cored)
steps: Heat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, mix together the maple syrup, ground cinnamon, and ground nutmeg.
In another small bowl, combine the oats, almond flour, vegetable oil, and chopped pecans. Mix until the crumbled topping is well combined.
Place the pear halves on a baking sheet, cut side up. Brush the cut sides of the pears with the maple syrup mixture.
Sprinkle the oat crumble mixture evenly over each pear half.
Roast the pears until the pears are tender and the crumble is golden brown, about 30 minutes. Serve warm.

title: Chicken Skewers with Peanut Sauce
description: These chicken skewers are tasty and versatile. Serve them with some veggies and brown rice for a fun and flavorful meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 250; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 85mg 28%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 29g; Potassium 400mg 9%
ingredients: 1 lbs boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into 1-inch thick strips)
steps: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning.

In a small bowl, whisk together kosher salt, black pepper, peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and turmeric. Add water gradually until you reach the desired sauce consistency.
Pour 1/3 of the peanut sauce on the chicken and stir well to coat the chicken in the marinade. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Preheat the grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Weave the chicken onto the skewers and grill for about 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F and has a nice char.
Drizzle the remaining peanut sauce over the top or serve it on the side for dipping.

title: Chicken Kofta with Tabbouleh
description: Filled with warm Middle Eastern flavors, this Persian dish was originally made with ground lamb. Ground chicken breast makes this a leaner, but still flavorful version. Paired with herby tabbouleh, hummus, and pita bread, you’ll feel like you are lounging by the Mediterranean Sea as you savor every bite.
serving_size: 4 chicken kofta + 1 1/4 cups tabbouleh + 2 Tbsp hummus + 1 small pita
nutrients_raw: Calories 390; Total Fat 13g 17%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 110mg 37%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 35g 13%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 36g; Potassium 620mg 13%
steps: To make the tabbouleh: Combine the bulgur wheat, ½ cup of the parsley, mint, 2 cloves of minced garlic, cucumbers, and tomatoes in a large bowl. Mix the lemon juice, lemon zest, and olive oil together in a small bowl. Drizzle the olive oil mixture over the bulgur and vegetables and toss to combine.
Cover tightly and place in the refrigerator until you are ready to serve. (You can make this ahead. The flavors will intensify as it chills.)

To make the chicken kofta: Place the chicken, egg, onion, 2 Tbsp chopped parsley, cumin, black pepper, 1 clove of minced garlic, and breadcrumbs in a large bowl. Mix them together with your hands or a couple of forks until all are well combined and evenly distributed. Divide the mixture and form into 16 small logs or roll into meatball shapes.

Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat and spray with cooking spray. Once hot, add the chicken rolls and cook on one side until browned. Continue turning to brown all sides and cooked through, about 10 minutes. They should reach an internal temperature of 165 degrees F on an instant-read thermometer.
Serve 4 kofta rolls on top of one lettuce leaf with 1 1/4 cups of tabbouleh, 2 Tbsp of hummus, and 1 small pita on the side.

title: Cold Cucumber Soup and Grilled Shrimp Open-Face Sandwich
description: Cool as a cucumber, this refreshing soup pairs perfectly with a grilled shrimp and spicy avocado aioli open-face sandwich. If the spice is too much, you can skip the hot sauce or just use a dash.
nutrients_raw: Calories 370; Total Fat 16g 21%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 100mg 33%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 29g 11%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 3g 6%; Protein 31g; Potassium 760mg 16%
ingredients: 2 med cucumber(s) (cut in thirds and in half lengthwise)
4 tbsp lemon juice (from 2 med lemons, divided)
steps: To make the soup, place half of the cucumbers in a food processor fit with the chopping blade. Process until it is cut into small pieces. Add the remaining cucumber sections and process until they are cut into small pieces.
Add the yogurt, lemon juice, lemon zest, and dill and process until liquified and all cucumber pieces are puréed.

Spray a grill pan or outdoor grill with cooking spray and heat to medium. Toss the shrimp with olive oil and black pepper. Place on the preheated grill and cook for 1 minute. Flip the shrimp and cook for an additional minute. Shrimp cooks quickly, so be careful not to overcook it. Remove it from the grill to a plate.
In a small bowl, mash the avocado and add the mayonnaise, lemon juice, and hot sauce, and mix until light green in color and the avocado is incorporated and smooth.
Spread 1 Tbsp of the avocado aioli over each slice of toast. Top with ¼ cup of arugula and 3 shrimp. Serve with 1 ¼ cup of the soup on the side.

title: Grilled Pork Tenderloin with Charred Romaine and Mango Salsa
serving_size: 4 oz pork + ½ cup quinoa + ¾ cup salsa + ½ head romaine lettuce
nutrients_raw: Calories 370; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 3g 15%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 80mg 27%; Sodium 230mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 36g 13%; Dietary Fiber 11g 39%; Total Sugars 11g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 34g; Potassium 1630mg 35%
ingredients: 2 head romaine lettuce (cut in half lengthwise, leave stem on)
steps: Place the pork tenderloin in a resealable plastic bag.

Combine the olive oil, ¼ cup of the lime juice, chili powder, cumin, honey, and cilantro in a small bowl. Pour over the pork tenderloin. Seal the bag and place it in the refrigerator to marinate for at least an hour, and no longer than 24 hours.
Meanwhile, prepare the quinoa according to the package directions. When done, fluff with a fork and let it cool slightly. Stir in the cheese just before serving.
To make the salsa, combine the mango, peppers, 1 Tbsp of lime juice, and lime zest. Set aside.

Preheat the grill to 450 degrees F. Remove the pork from the marinade and place it on the grill. Cook, turning occasionally to sear all sides. The pork is done when it reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees F, about 10 minutes.

During the last 5 minutes of grilling, spray each romaine half lightly with cooking spray. Place on the grill grates and cook until the lettuce is just starting to char and wilt. Remove and place on a plate. Top with the mango salsa.
Slice the pork and serve over the quinoa with the romaine and mango salsa.

title: Herbed Roasted Cod and Roasted Summer Vegetables Over Quinoa
description: Cod is a mild white fish that takes on the flavors it cooks with. This bold spice mix adds a peppery Mediterranean flavor to the fish and vegetables. Enjoy it with a side of quinoa or another whole grain. This recipe can easily be doubled to feed the whole family.
serving_size: ⅓ cup quinoa + 1 cup vegetables + 6 oz cod
nutrients_raw: Calories 390; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 42g 15%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 12g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 28g; Potassium 1000mg 21%
steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Line a sheet pan or baking sheet with aluminum foil or parchment paper.
Place the tomatoes, squash, zucchini, onion, garlic cloves, and walnuts in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, mix the olive oil, basil, oregano, parsley, red pepper, and black pepper.
Add 2 tsp of the olive oil and 2 tsp of the spice blend onto the vegetables and toss to coat.
Divide the last tsp of the olive oil and last tsp of the spice blend between the cod fillets and spread over the top.

Place the cod on one end of the baking sheet and spread the vegetables over the other end. Roast in the oven until the cod reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees F or until the fish easily flakes apart with a fork and is no longer translucent, about 20 minutes.
While the cod and vegetables are roasting, prepare the quinoa according to package directions.

title: Mason Jar Pho Soup
description: If you are looking for a quick, grab-and-go lunch that is anything but ordinary, this Mason Jar Pho Soup will hit the spot. To save time, you can make a few of these jars ahead and enjoy them throughout the week. Look for instant rice noodles for this soup. If you can’t find instant noodles, parboil (briefly boil) regular rice noodles and spray them with a little cooking spray before packing them in the jar. In place of bouillon, use no-salt-added beef broth.
serving_size: 3 oz beef + 2 cup vegetables + 1 oz noodles + 1 cup broth
nutrients_raw: Calories 290; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2.5g 13%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 260mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 32g 12%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 25g; Potassium 1040mg 22%
ingredients: 3 oz lean steak (cooked, sliced into thin strips)
steps: Use a large (24 to 32 oz-wide mouth) mason jar with a tight-sealing lid.

Layer the dry ingredients as follows in the jar: bouillon (if using), ginger root, rice noodles, cooked beef, mushrooms, peppers, cabbage, carrots, green onion, and cilantro. Seal tightly and place in the refrigerator until ready to use.
In a separate small container, mix the soy sauce and lime juice and place in the refrigerator.

When you are ready to prepare the soup, remove the jar from the fridge at least 15 minutes before preparing it. Heat a cup of warm water (or beef broth) in the microwave until boiling. Stir in the soy sauce and lime juice.

Pour the water and soy sauce mixture into the jar and seal it tightly again. Swish it around to make sure the noodles are covered in liquid. Allow it to sit for 2-3 minutes or until the noodles are softened. Alternatively, heat the water (or broth) in a medium saucepan until boiling. Pour the ingredients from the jar into the saucepan and stir until combined and the noodles soften. Pour into a bowl to enjoy.

title: Mediterranean Vegan Breakfast Bowl
description: Turmeric gives the scrambled tofu a rich yellow color that mimics the look of scrambled eggs and combining it with the garlic powder adds a zesty, savory bite. This filling breakfast bowl is a great way to add vegetables and whole grains to your morning.
nutrients_raw: Calories 400; Total Fat 19g 24%; Saturated Fat 3g 15%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 39g 14%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 25g; Potassium 730mg 16%
ingredients: 2 sprays, 0.5 g nonstick cooking spray (olive oil)
steps: Spray a medium-sized skillet with cooking spray. Place the tofu in the skillet and break it apart with a fork or potato masher. Mix in the turmeric, garlic powder, salt, and 2 Tbsp almond milk. Cook over medium-low heat until warmed through.

In a small bowl, combine the tahini, yogurt, lemon juice, and 1 Tbsp almond milk and mix until combined and the tahini has thinned to a dressing consistency. You can add a little more milk or lemon juice if needed.
Place half of the cauliflower rice and quinoa in a bowl and mix to combine. Add half of the carrots and radishes to the bowl. Repeat with the second bowl.
Spray the kale with the olive oil cooking spray. Rub it into the kale until it is softened and bright green in color. Add half the kale to each bowl.
Divide the scrambled tofu and add half alongside the kale and other vegetables. Drizzle with the dressing.

title: Pesto Pasta Tuna Salad
description: This herby pasta salad gets an extra boost with a pantry staple, tuna. No-salt-added albacore tuna helps keep the sodium content down and allows the pesto and vegetables to shine through. Albacore tuna has a firm texture like chicken breast and a mild flavor.
serving_size: 2 cup pasta salad + 2 oz tuna + 2 cups mixed greens
nutrients_raw: Calories 400; Total Fat 16g 21%; Saturated Fat 3g 15%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 30mg 10%; Sodium 400mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 41g 15%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 27g; Potassium 790mg 17%
ingredients: 2 (4.5 oz) cans tuna packed in water (solid, no salt added, drained)
steps: Cook the pasta according to the package directions to the al dente stage.

While the pasta is cooking, place the chopped kale in a large bowl and drizzle it with olive oil. Gently rub the oil into the pieces of kale until they soften slightly and turn dark green. Add the zucchini, pepper, and tomatoes to the bowl and toss.

Once the pasta is done, drain it and add it to the vegetables and toss well. Stir in the pesto until the pasta is coated. Cover it tightly and place it in the refrigerator to chill for at least an hour.
Just before serving, gently break apart the tuna and mix it into the pasta and vegetables, coating it with pesto.
Place 2 cups of mixed greens on a plate or a bowl. Top with 2 cups of the pesto pasta tuna.

title: Salmon and Spring Veggie Breakfast Casserole
description: This zesty spring breakfast casserole can be made with canned salmon or is a great way to use up leftover fresh salmon. If using canned salmon, look for the option with the lowest sodium. This casserole can be made ahead and reheated, making it perfect for brunch.
serving_size: 1 wedge of casserole + 1 slice of toast
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2.5g 13%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 110mg 37%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 29g 11%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 25g; Potassium 440mg 9%
ingredients: 1 lbs asparagus (about 16 spears, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces)
6 large egg whites (or 3/4 cup egg substitute)
3/4 cup cottage cheese (reduced fat, reduced sodium)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Spray a 9x13-inch casserole dish with cooking spray.

Place the asparagus, peas, and broccoli in a medium saucepan with about 1 inch of water. Cover and bring to a boil and cook for about 2 minutes, or until the vegetables are bright green and just slightly tender. Drain and place the vegetables in a bowl of ice water to cool quickly. Once cold, drain well, mix in the red bell pepper, and spread the vegetables out in the prepared casserole. Distribute the salmon pieces over the vegetables.

In a medium bowl, beat the egg whites and eggs on medium speed for about 1 minute. The mixture should be slightly bubbly. Add the cottage cheese, dill, black pepper, and lemon juice and beat on medium speed for another minute to break up the cheese and combine.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and salmon. Top with mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, until the egg mixture is firm and no liquid remains. An inserted knife or toothpick should come out clean.
Cut into 6 pieces, garnish with fresh microgreens if desired, and serve with a slice of toast.

title: Baked Chai Banana Chips
description: These Baked Chai Banana Chips make for a tasty and healthy snack with a delightful chai spice twist. The natural sweetness of bananas combined with the warm chai spices creates a satisfying and aromatic snack.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 0g 0%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 0mg 0%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 12g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 366mg 8%
steps: Preheat your oven to 200 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Peel the bananas and slice them into thin rounds, approximately 1/8- to ¼-inch thick. Place the banana slices in a bowl and toss them with lemon juice to prevent browning and adds a touch of tartness.
In a small bowl, mix the ground cinnamon, ground cardamom, ground ginger, ground cloves, and ground nutmeg to create a chai spice blend.

Sprinkle the chai spice blend over the banana slices, ensuring they are well coated with the aromatic spices. Arrange the banana slices on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer, making sure they do not overlap.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 2 hours, or until the banana chips are crispy and golden brown. Flip the chips halfway through the baking time to ensure even crispiness.

Keep an eye on the banana chips towards the end of the baking time to prevent burning. The exact baking time may vary depending on your oven and the thickness of the slices. They will continue to crisp up as they cool.
Store the banana chips in an airtight container at room temperature after allowing to cool completely.

title: Salt and Pepper Roasted Edamame
description: Salt and Pepper Roasted Edamame is not only a tasty and crunchy snack, but also a nutritious one. Edamame is rich in protein and fiber, making it a healthy option for those looking for a satisfying and wholesome treat.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 0g 0%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 300mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 9g; Potassium 330mg 7%
ingredients: 2 cup fresh shelled edamame (thawed, no salt added)
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, toss the thawed edamame with olive oil until they are evenly coated.
Spread the edamame in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Sprinkle sea salt and black pepper evenly over the edamame. Toss to ensure the seasoning is well distributed.

Roast in the preheated oven for about 15 minutes or until the edamame is slightly crispy, stirring once or twice during the cooking time for even roasting. If you like a bit of heat, sprinkle red pepper flakes over the roasted edamame before serving.
Remove from the oven and let the edamame cool slightly before serving.

title: Whipped Cottage Cheese Dip
description: Whipped Cottage Cheese Dip is a light and creamy alternative to traditional dips, providing a protein-packed option for snacking. Enjoy with your favorite veggies like broccoli, bell pepper, carrots, and more!
nutrients_raw: Calories 50; Total Fat 1.5g 2%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 230mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 7g; Potassium 104mg 2%
steps: In a blender or food processor, combine the low-fat cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, fresh lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and minced garlic. Blend the ingredients until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. This may take a few minutes, depending on the power of your blender or food processor.
Once the mixture is smooth, transfer it to a bowl. Stir in the chopped fresh chives and season the whipped cottage cheese dip with pepper. Mix well to ensure the flavors are evenly distributed.
Refrigerate the dip for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld and enhance the overall taste.

title: Roasted Cauliflower Hummus
description: Roasted Cauliflower Hummus is a delicious twist on traditional hummus, incorporating the rich, nutty flavor of roasted cauliflower. The roasted cauliflower adds depth and richness, making it a delicious and health-conscious option for snacks, appetizers, or as a spread for sandwiches and wraps.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 240mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 451mg 10%
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F.
Toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil and spread them on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast in the preheated oven for about 25 minutes or until the cauliflower is tender and golden brown, stirring halfway through. Allow the roasted cauliflower to cool for a few minutes.

In a food processor, combine the roasted cauliflower, minced garlic, tahini, lemon juice, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Pulse the mixture until it starts to break down, then scrape down the sides of the food processor.
With the food processor running, add water gradually until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. You may need to stop and scrape down the sides of the processor a couple of times.
Serve topped with chopped, fresh parsley and a sprinkle of smoke paprika for garnish.

title: Green Pea Hummus
description: Green Pea Hummus is a vibrant and refreshing twist on traditional hummus, incorporating the sweetness and bright green color of peas. It's a great option for spring and summer gatherings or any time you want a unique and tasty variation of traditional hummus.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 140mg 3%
ingredients: 1/2 cup canned chickpeas (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a food processor, combine the thawed green peas, chickpeas, fresh mint, tahini, fresh lemon juice, minced garlic, olive oil, ground cumin, salt, and pepper. Pulse the mixture until the ingredients start to break down.

With the food processor running, add water gradually until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. You may need to stop and scrape down the sides of the processor a couple of times. Taste and adjust the seasoning if necessary.

title: Roasted Pepper and White Bean Dip
description: This Roasted Pepper and White Bean Dip is a flavorful and creamy appetizer that combines the smokiness of roasted peppers with the mildness of white beans. It makes a great addition to your appetizer spread or as a flavorful dip for various snacks.
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 231mg 5%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans (drained and rinsed)
1 (8 oz) jar) roasted red peppers (chopped, liquid reserved)
steps: In a food processor, combine the white beans, roasted and chopped red bell peppers, olive oil, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.

Pulse the mixture until it starts to break down. With the food processor running, add juice from the roasted red peppers gradually until you achieve a smooth and creamy consistency. You may need to stop and scrape down the sides of the processor a couple of times.

title: Trail Mix with Pepitas and Cranberries
description: This trail mix is a versatile and portable snack that's perfect for hiking, camping, or anytime you need a quick and tasty boost.
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 120mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 15g 5%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 200mg 4%
ingredients: 3/4 cup pepitas (pumpkin seeds) (raw, no added salt)
steps: In a large dry skillet over medium heat, toast the raw pepitas, almonds, and walnuts for about 3–5 minutes, or until they become fragrant and lightly browned. Stir frequently to prevent burning.
Remove the toasted pepitas and nuts from the skillet and let them cool completely.

In a large bowl, combine the toasted pepitas, almonds, and walnuts with the sunflower seeds, unsweetened dried cranberries, ground cinnamon, and sea salt. Toss all the ingredients together until they are well combined.
Portion the trail mix into ⅓-cup individual servings or store it in an airtight container for later use.

title: Pesto Deviled Eggs
description: Pesto Deviled Eggs are a flavorful and elegant twist on the classic recipe. The combination of pesto, mayonnaise, and Dijon mustard creates a creamy and zesty filling that pairs wonderfully with the natural richness of hard-boiled eggs. These deviled eggs make a great appetizer for parties or a tasty addition to your brunch spread.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 330mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 1.99mg <1%
steps: Place the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10–12 minutes.
Transfer the boiled eggs to an ice water bath to cool.
Once the eggs are cool, peel them and cut them in half lengthwise. Remove the yolks and place them in a bowl.
In the bowl with the egg yolks, add mayonnaise, prepared basil pesto, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Mash and mix the ingredients together until smooth.
Spoon or pipe the pesto filling into the hollowed-out egg whites.
Chill the deviled eggs in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.

title: Sriracha Deviled Eggs
description: Sriracha Deviled Eggs are a bold and spicy twist on a classic favorite. They make a fantastic appetizer for spice lovers and add a fiery kick to your party or gathering. Enjoy these zesty deviled eggs as a delicious and diabetes-friendly snack.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 340mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 10mg <1%
ingredients: 1 stalks green onion (scallion) (thinly sliced, for garnish)
steps: Place the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10–12 minutes.
Transfer the boiled eggs to an ice water bath to cool.
Once the eggs are cool, peel them and cut them in half lengthwise. Remove the yolks and place them in a bowl.

In the bowl with the egg yolks, add mayonnaise, Sriracha sauce, Dijon mustard, rice vinegar, salt, and pepper. Mash and mix the ingredients together until smooth. Spoon or pipe the Sriracha filling into the hollowed-out egg whites.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving. Top with sliced scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Curry Deviled Eggs
description: Curried Deviled Eggs are a delightful appetizer that brings a touch of spice and warmth to your table. The combination of curry powder, Dijon mustard, and apple cider vinegar creates a flavorful and aromatic filling that's sure to be a hit at parties and gatherings. Enjoy these uniquely seasoned deviled eggs!
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 5mg <1%
steps: Place the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10–12 minutes.
Transfer the boiled eggs to an ice water bath to cool.
Once the eggs are cool, peel them and cut them in half lengthwise. Remove the yolks and place them in a bowl.

In the bowl with the egg yolks, add mayonnaise, curry powder, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper. Mash and mix the ingredients together until smooth. Spoon or pipe the curry filling into the hollowed-out egg whites.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving. Sprinkle lightly with paprika and top with fresh dill if desired.

title: Dill and Pickle Deviled Eggs
description: Dill and Pickle Deviled Eggs offer a delightful combination of tangy pickles, fresh dill, and the classic deviled egg filling. They make a flavorful and crowd-pleasing appetizer for picnics, parties, or any occasion. Enjoy these zesty deviled eggs with a unique and herby twist!
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 270mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 5mg <1%
ingredients: 2 tbsp dill pickles (no added sugar, finely chopped)
steps: Place the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover them with water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water to cool. Peel the eggs when they are cool enough to handle.
Cut the peeled hard-boiled eggs in half lengthwise and carefully remove the yolks.

Place the yolks in a bowl and mash them with a fork. To the mashed yolks, add low-fat mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, chopped dill pickles, pickle juice, fresh dill, salt, and pepper. Mix everything together until well combined.
Spoon or pipe the yolk mixture back into the egg white halves. You can use a plastic bag with the corner snipped off to pipe the filling for a neater look.
Refrigerate the deviled eggs for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld. Garnish with more fresh dill.

title: Ranch Deviled Eggs
description: Ranch Deviled Eggs are a tasty and familiar twist on the classic recipe, making them a great addition to picnics, potlucks, or any occasion. Enjoy the creamy and herby goodness of ranch dressing in each bite!
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 185mg 62%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 1g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 2mg <1%
ingredients: 1 tbsp ranch-flavored salad dressing powder mix
steps: Place the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover them with water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water to cool. Peel the eggs when they are cool enough to handle.
Cut the peeled hard-boiled eggs in half lengthwise and carefully remove the yolks.

Place the yolks in a bowl and mash them with a fork. To the mashed yolks, add ¼ cup low-fat mayonnaise, 1 teaspoon of Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon ranch dressing mix. Mix everything together until well combined and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Once the filling is ready, spoon or pipe it back into the egg white halves. Consider using a plastic bag with the corner snipped off for a neater look.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld. Sprinkle lightly with paprika. Serve chilled and enjoy these delicious, diabetes-friendly appetizers or snacks.

title: Fish Cake Sliders
description: These Fish Cake Sliders are perfect for a snack or as party appetizers. The crispy fish cakes paired with fresh toppings and soft slider buns create a delightful combination of flavors and textures. Enjoy these sliders for a tasty seafood treat!
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 320mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 13g 5%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 16g; Potassium 269mg 6%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can canned salmon (no salt added, drained, flaked)
steps: In a large bowl, gently mix the salmon (including 2 tablespoons of the can liquid), breadcrumbs, green onion, garlic, flour, egg, old bay seasoning, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Form 8 patties, about ½-inch thick.
In a non-stick skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Cook the fish cakes for about 3–4 minutes on each side or until they are golden brown and cooked through.
While the fish cakes are cooking, slice the whole grain slider buns. Once the fish cakes are done, place them on the prepared slider buns.
Add a fresh lettuce leaf to each slider. If desired, include a sliced tomatoes for extra flavor and texture. Spread a thin layer of light tartar sauce on each.

title: Asparagus and Leek Frittata
description: Revitalize your breakfast routine with this Asparagus and Leek Frittata, a delicious and nutritious choice for a vibrant start to your day. This frittata combines the crisp freshness of asparagus and the mild sweetness of leeks, creating a flavorful symphony that's both friendly to people with diabetes and a protein-packed way to start your morning.
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 3g 4%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 9g; Potassium 224mg 5%
ingredients: 1 cup leeks (thoroughly washed, white and pale green parts, chopped)
1 bunch (about 2 1/2 cups) asparagus (trimmed, cut on diagonal into 1-inch pieces)
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Whisk egg substitute, milk, cheeses, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl and set aside.
Add olive oil to heavy oven-proof 10-inch cast iron or nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Add leeks and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add asparagus and sauté until tender, about 6 minutes, stirring often so leeks brown evenly.
Add egg mixture to skillet, folding gently to combine. Allow edges to set, then place into a preheated oven and bake for 10–15 minutes until frittata is puffed and golden.
Cut into 8 wedges and serve.

title: Pineapple Coconut Greek Yogurt
description: Transform your breakfast into a tropical delight with our Fresh Pineapple Coconut Greek Yogurt Parfait—a delicious and diabetes-friendly option to kickstart your day. This parfait combines the luscious sweetness of fresh pineapple with the creamy richness of coconut-infused Greek yogurt. For extra flavor and crunch, toast the sliced almonds in the oven beforehand.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 65mg 3%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 13g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 21g; Potassium 393mg 8%
ingredients: 2 tsp low-calorie sugar substitute (no added sugar)
steps: In a small bowl, mix the Greek yogurt, sugar substitute, and coconut extract. Adjust the sweetness to your taste.
In serving glasses or bowls, begin by adding a layer yogurt mixture.
Add a layer of pineapple on top of the yogurt.
Sprinkle the almonds over the pineapple.
Repeat the layers until your glass is filled. Serve cold.

title: Avocado and Tomato Breakfast Toast
description: For a quick and easy breakfast, try this Avocado and Tomato Breakfast Toast. Creamy avocado pairs with juicy tomato and eggs for a protein-rich start to your day. You can add an extra kick of flavor with a dash of hot sauce or siracha on your toast.
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 21g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 11g; Potassium 496mg 11%
steps: Start by preparing the avocado spread. Cut the ripe avocado in half, remove the pit, and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Mash it with a fork and season with 1/8 teaspoon salt. You can also add a dash of hot sauce if desired.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and use cooking spray.
While the skillet is heating, toast the slices of whole grain bread until they are golden brown.

In the heated skillet, crack the eggs and cook them to your preference (e.g., fried, scrambled, or poached). Season with 1/8 teaspoon salt and pepper to taste. If you prefer your eggs with runny yolks, cook them for about 2–3 minutes sunny side up or a bit longer for over easy.

Assemble the toast. Spread the mashed avocado on each slice of toasted bread and add a layer of sliced tomatoes on top. Place the cooked eggs on the tomato slices. Sprinkle black pepper over the top if desired.

title: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
description: These tasty Cottage Cheese Pancakes are packed with protein to keep you fueled through the morning. Top them with some fresh berries for a bright start to your morning.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 145mg 48%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 18g 7%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 22g; Potassium 237mg 5%
ingredients: 2 cup cottage cheese (low fat, no added salt)
steps: In a blender or food processor, combine the low-fat cottage cheese, eggs, whole wheat flour, baking powder, vanilla extract, sugar substitute, and salt. Blend until the mixture is smooth and well combined.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat and lightly grease it with cooking spray or a small amount of oil.
Pour pancake batter onto the skillet to create pancakes of your desired size (usually about 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake).
Cook the pancakes for about 2–3 minutes on one side or until you see small bubbles forming on the surface and the edges start to set.
Flip the pancakes and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes on the other side or until they are golden brown and cooked through.
Remove the pancakes from the skillet and keep them warm while you cook the remaining batter.

title: Almond Flour Pancakes
description: Enjoy your morning with these Gluten-Free Almond Flour Pancakes that provide enough protein to keep you powered.
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 15g 19%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 320mg 7%
steps: In a bowl, whisk together almond flour, gluten free flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, beat the egg substitute and add almond milk, canola oil, sugar free maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Mix well.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until combined. Let the batter sit for a couple of minutes to thicken.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat and grease with cooking spray.
Pour ¼ cup of batter onto the skillet for each pancake. Spread the batter slightly with the back of a spoon.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface, then flip and cook until the other side is golden brown.
Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve topped with one fresh, sliced strawberry.

title: Cottage Cheese and Veggie Wrap
description: Try a new way to eat cottage cheese with these delicious and easy Cottage Cheese and Veggie Wraps. If you want to add a punch of flavor, try drizzling on a bit of balsamic glaze before rolling up the wraps.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 12g; Potassium 358mg 8%
ingredients: 1 cup cottage cheese (no salt added, low fat)
1/4 cup fresh herbs (such as dill, basil, parsley, chopped)
steps: Lay out the tortillas on a clean surface.
Evenly spread the cottage cheese on each tortilla.
Distribute the cherry tomatoes, cucumber slices, red onion, and bell peppers over the cottage cheese.
Sprinkle the fresh herbs on top.
Season with the salt and pepper.
Fold in the sides of the tortillas and then roll them up tightly to create wraps.

title: Cottage Cheese and Berry Stuffed Crepes
description: Craving something sweet and savory for breakfast? Make these Cottage Cheese and Berry Stuffed Crepes! They’re rich in protein which will help keep you full all morning long.
nutrients_raw: Calories 280; Total Fat 15g 19%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 470mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 23g; Potassium 332mg 7%
steps: Make the crepes. In a blender, combine almond flour, coconut flour, eggs, almond milk, olive oil, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Blend until smooth
Allow the crepe batter to rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and lightly spray with cooking spray.
Pour a small amount of batter into the skillet, swirling it to coat the bottom thinly and evenly.
Cook each crepe for about 1–2 minutes on each side or until lightly golden. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Spoon the cottage cheese onto one half of each crepe.
Add a layer of mixed berries over the cottage cheese.
Fold in the sides and roll to close each crepe around the filling.

title: Mushroom Frittata
description: Earthy mushrooms are the start of this diabetes-friendly frittata. Frittatas are egg based dishes, a cross between an omelet and a crustless quiche.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 470mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 6g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 16g; Potassium 360mg 8%
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
In a bowl, whisk the egg substitute with salt, pepper, and dried thyme.
Heat the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add in the diced onions and cook until softened.
Add the sliced mushrooms to the skillet and cook until they release their moisture, about 6 minutes.
Pour in the whisked eggs over the mushroom mixture.
Allow the edges of the frittata to set, lifting them with a spatula to let the uncooked eggs flow underneath.
Once the edges are set, sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese evenly over the top.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for about 10–12 minutes or until the frittata is cooked through and the top is golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before slicing.

title: Cranberry Pumpkin Muffins
description: Cranberry Pumpkin Muffins are a great way to enjoy the flavors of fall. Slightly sweet pumpkin and tart cranberries pair perfectly for this diabetes-friendly muffin recipe.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 192mg 4%
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a muffin tin with paper liners.
In a large bowl, whisk together the almond flour, coconut flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and salt.
In another bowl, whisk together the pumpkin purée, almond milk, eggs, ​applesauce​​​, almond butter, and sugar substitute until well combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Gently fold in the cranberries.
Spoon the batter evenly into the muffin cups, filling each about 2/3 full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 18–20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Allow the muffins to cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Cinnamon Apple Overnight Oats
description: Overnight oats are a great way to prepare a grab-and-go breakfast the night before. Simply add the ingredients to a bowl and let it sit in the fridge overnight for a delicious and nutritious start to your day! This Cinnamon Apple version is great when enjoyed in the fall.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 10g; Potassium 343mg 7%
steps: In a bowl or jar, combine rolled oats, almond milk, Greek yogurt, chopped apple, chopped nuts, maple syrup, ground cinnamon, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Stir well.
Cover the bowl or jar and refrigerate overnight or for at least 8 hours.
In the morning, give the overnight oats a good stir.
Adjust the consistency with additional almond milk if desired.

title: Cottage Cheese with Pineapple and Walnuts
description: Take your cottage cheese to the next level with this recipe! Top with mint leaves for extra freshness.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 270mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 18g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 10g; Potassium 278mg 6%
steps: In a bowl, combine the cottage cheese, fresh pineapple chunks, and chopped walnuts.
Divide the cottage cheese mixture into serving bowls. Serve immediately and enjoy this refreshing and protein-packed dish.

title: Roasted Veggie Quinoa Bowl
description: This Roasted Veggie Quinoa Bowl is a satisfying delight, easy enough to put together for lunch or dinner. Make it colorful by adding your favorite veggies to the mix. Serve with fresh lemon wedges for a burst of citrus flavor.
serving_size: ½ cup cooked quinoa + 3 oz chicken + 1 cup veggies + ½ Tbsp feta
nutrients_raw: Calories 350; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 220mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 37g 13%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 23g; Potassium 830mg 18%
ingredients: 4 cup mixed, nonstarchy vegetables (bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, zucchini, broccoli, etc.)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a saucepan, combine the dry quinoa with 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Cover, and simmer for 15 minutes or until quinoa is cooked and water is absorbed.
While the quinoa is cooking, spread the cubed chicken and chopped vegetables on a baking sheet.
Drizzle olive oil over the chicken and vegetables, sprinkle with the dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Roast the chicken and vegetables in the preheated oven for about 20–25 minutes or until they are tender and slightly browned and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.
Assemble by dividing the cooked quinoa and roasted vegetable mix among bowls.
Top with crumbled feta cheese and serve with fresh lemon wedges.

title: Crispy Parmesan Chicken
description: This recipe provides a deliciously crispy crust with the rich flavor of Parmesan cheese. Serve the chicken with your favorite sides, such as roasted vegetables, salad, or try low-carb veggie noodles.
nutrients_raw: Calories 270; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 70mg 23%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 20g 7%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 29g; Potassium 283.01mg 6%
ingredients: 4 whole boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 4 oz each)
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F.
Season both sides of the chicken breasts with kosher salt and black pepper.
Add the flour to a shallow bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs.
In a shallow dish, combine the Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, dried oregano, dried basil, and breadcrumbs.
Dredge each chicken breast in the flour, eggs, and lastly the Parmesan mixture, coating evenly. Set on a plate and repeat with the remaining chicken breasts.
Heat the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken breasts to the skillet and sear for 2–3 minutes on one side until golden brown.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for about 15–18 minutes or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 165 degrees F.

title: Crispy Chicken Thighs with Spinach and Shallots
description: This dish combines the richness of crispy chicken thighs with the freshness of sautéed spinach and shallots for a well-balanced and flavorful dinner option.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 140mg 47%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 32g; Potassium 427mg 9%
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season both sides with kosher salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the chicken thighs in the skillet. Cook until the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees F, about 6 minutes per side. Remove to a plate and cover with foil to keep the chicken warm.
In the same skillet, sauté the sliced shallots until softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken broth and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the fresh baby spinach to the skillet and cook, stirring until wilted.
Serve the crispy chicken thighs on the bed of sautéed spinach and shallot mixture.

title: Lentil and Turkey Stuffed Peppers
description: These stuffed peppers are a well-balanced meal, combining the protein from lentils and turkey with the vibrant flavors of veggies and spices. They make for a satisfying and diabetes-friendly dinner option.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 290mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 509mg 11%
ingredients: 1 (14 oz) can canned diced tomatoes (no salt added, drained)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
In a medium saucepan, combine the lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 20–25 minutes or until lentils are tender. Drain any excess liquid.
While lentils are cooking, place the halved bell peppers in a baking dish. Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes until softened.
In a large skillet over medium heat, add the chopped onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic to the skillet, then the ground turkey. Cook until browned and barely cooked through.
Stir in the ground cumin, smoked paprika, dried oregano, kosher salt, and black pepper.
Add the cooked lentils, diced tomatoes, and 1/2 cup of shredded mozzarella to the skillet. Stir until well combined.
Spoon the lentil and turkey mixture into each softened bell pepper half.
Top each stuffed pepper with the remaining shredded mozzarella.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake for 20–25 minutes or until the peppers are fully cooked through.
Remove the foil and broil for an additional 3–5 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.  Garnish with fresh parsley if desired

title: Lemon Garlic Shrimp Skewers
description: These Lemon Garlic Shrimp Skewers are versatile and can be served alongside a salad, over brown rice, or with your favorite veggies. The combination of lemon and garlic adds a bright and savory kick to the grilled shrimp.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 170mg 57%; Sodium 360mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 2g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 20g; Potassium 248mg 5%
steps: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 15 minutes to prevent burning during grilling.
Zest and juice one of the lemons. Thinly slice the other.
In a bowl, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, dried oregano, rosemary, and black pepper.
Add the peeled and deveined shrimp to the marinade, making sure they are well coated. Let them marinate for at least 15 minutes
Preheat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Thread the marinated shrimp onto the skewers, along with one or two lemon slices per skewer.
Place the shrimp skewers on the preheated grill and cook for about 2–3 minutes per side or until the shrimp are fully cooked and develop a light char.

title: Sweet and Sour Baked Chicken
description: This dish offers a delightful balance of sweet and tangy flavors, and baking the chicken provides a lighter alternative to frying. It's a family-friendly meal that's sure to be a hit at the dinner table.
nutrients_raw: Calories 300; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 140mg 47%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 22g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 14g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 31g; Potassium 650mg 14%
ingredients: 4 thighs boneless skinless chicken thighs (about 4 oz each)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Season the chicken thighs with black pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together the pineapple juice, ketchup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, and cornstarch until well combined. Set aside.
In an oven-safe skillet or baking dish, heat the canola oil over medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs and sear until golden brown, about 3–4 minutes per side.
Pour the prepared sweet and sour sauce over the chicken, ensuring each piece is well coated.
Scatter sliced red and green bell peppers, as well as pineapple chunks, around the chicken in the skillet.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for approximately 25 minutes or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F and the sauce is bubbly and thickened.
Remove from the oven and let it rest for a few minutes.
Garnish with the sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds

title: Green Chili Chicken Casserole
description: This Green Chili Chicken Casserole is a crowd-pleaser, and the combination of green chilies, chicken, and cheese creates a comforting and delicious dish. It’s perfect for an easy weeknight dinner the whole family can enjoy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 40mg 13%; Sodium 270mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 19g; Potassium 338mg 7%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans (no salt added, rinsed and drained)
3/4 cup shredded Mexican cheese blend (low fat)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Spray a 9-inch square baking dish with cooking spray.
In a large bowl, combine chopped chicken, black beans, diced green chilies, red bell pepper, Greek yogurt, salsa verde, ground cumin, garlic powder, and black pepper. Mix until well combined.
Spoon the chicken mixture into the baking dish, spreading it out evenly.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese over the top.
Cover the casserole with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake until the casserole is hot and bubbly and the cheese is melted and golden brown, about 10 minutes more.
Remove from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before slicing into 8 squares. Top with chopped, fresh cilantro.

title: Shrimp and Grits Stuffed Pepper
