description: Try this twist on the classic shrimp and grits. This lower carb recipe is a great option for people with diabetes and packs a ton of flavor into an easy weeknight dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 210; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 90mg 30%; Sodium 450mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 17g; Potassium 355mg 8%
ingredients: 1 cup cheddar cheese (reduced fat, shredded, divided)
steps: Cook the grits according to the package instructions until creamy and smooth.
Fold in ½ cup cheddar cheese, 1/8 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp black pepper.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Place the halved bell peppers in a baking dish, cut side up. Cover and bake for 40 minutes.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion and garlic, sauté until softened.
Stir in the cherry tomatoes, Old Bay seasoning, remaining kosher salt, and pepper. Cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and add the shrimp to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Spoon the cooked grits into each pepper half, pressing down with the back of the spoon. Top the grits with the shrimp and tomato mixture.
Sprinkle the remaining shredded cheddar cheese over each stuffed pepper.
Cover with foil and bake until the cheese is melted, the peppers have softened, and the filling is cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Broil for 2-3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly.
Remove from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired.

title: Grilled Steak and Vegetable Kebabs
description: Pull out the grill for these delicious kebabs. These are diabetes-friendly and packed with non-starchy veggies which makes it a tasty choice the whole family will enjoy.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 105mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 20g; Potassium 601mg 13%
ingredients: 12 oz lean top sirloin steak (trimmed, cut into 1-inch cubes)
steps: In a bowl, mix together ½ tablespoon olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, smoked paprika, ¼ teaspoon black pepper. Add the steak and stir well to coat the meat in the oil and spices.
In another bowl, toss the vegetables with ½ tablespoon olive oil, 1/8 teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper.
Thread the marinated steak cubes, zucchini slices, red onion wedges, and cherry tomatoes onto the skewers, alternating for variety.
Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.

Place the kebabs on the preheated grill. Grill, turning occasionally, until the steak reaches your desired level of doneness and the vegetables are tender with a slight char, about 8 minutes, for medium.
Remove the kebabs from the grill and let them rest for a few minutes before serving.

title: Moroccan Salmon
description: Add some exotic flair to your salmon dinner with this diabetes-friendly recipe. If you can’t find pomegranate molasses in your grocery store, you can swap it with balsamic vinegar instead.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 55mg 18%; Sodium 320mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 4g 8%; Protein 21g; Potassium 376mg 8%
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk together the pomegranate molasses (or balsamic vinegar), white miso paste, lemon juice, and pepper.
Place the salmon filets on the prepared baking sheet. Brush the pomegranate mixture over the salmon, making sure to coat each filet. Top each fillet with a fresh thyme sprig.
Bake the salmon in the preheated oven for about 12–15 minutes, or until the salmon is cooked through to 145 degrees F.
Remove the salmon from the oven and garnish with pomegranate arils.

title: Blackened Fish with Street Corn Style Salsa
description: Spice up dinner with this quick and easy Blacked Fish with Street Corn Style Salsa. Using a homemade blend of spices and fresh ingredients, this diabetes-friendly meal comes together in under 30 minutes!
nutrients_raw: Calories 340; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 100mg 33%; Sodium 350mg 15%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 44g; Potassium 662mg 14%
steps: Make your spice mixture by combining the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, thyme, cumin, chili powder, ground oregano, cayenne pepper (if using) and kosher salt in a small bowl.
Pat the fish filets dry with a paper towel and season evenly on both sides with the spice mix.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat with the 2 tablespoons of oil. When the oil shimmers, gently lay the fish fillets in the pan, presentation side down.

Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the spice mixture is fragrant and beginning to color. Flip the fish and cook for an additional 3 to 4 minutes, depending on the thickness of the filets. Set aside and cover with foil.

Pour the avocado oil into the same pan you cooked the fish in and turn the heat up to high. Once the oil is hot and shimmering, add the corn and cook until it starts to blister and brown, about 5 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onion and jalapeno. Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes or until the onions get translucent and the whole thing is aromatic.
Turn the heat off and stir in the chili powder, kosher salt, lime zest and juice. Add the chopped cilantro.
Top the fish with the corn salsa and fresh cilantro prior to serving.

title: Miso Glazed Salmon
description: Add some Asian-inspired flair to your salmon with this delicious miso glaze. Salmon is rich in omega-3 fatty acids, making it a nutritious choice for people with diabetes.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 45mg 15%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 20g; Potassium 245mg 5%
ingredients: 2 (3 oz) fillets sockeye salmon (boneless, skin on)
steps: Whisk the maple syrup, miso, vinegar, red pepper flakes, and orange zest and juice in a small bowl to combine.

Spray a medium nonstick skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Place the salmon in the skillet—skin side down—and cook until the skin is very crisp and deep golden brown, 7–9 minutes. Continue to cook until it’s very lightly browned on the flesh side and registers 145 degrees F on an instant read thermometer, approximately 2 minutes.
Add the glaze. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the glaze begins to thicken, about 2 minutes.
Place salmon on plates and garnish with any remaining glaze from the pan.

title: Kale Salad with Warm Cherry Shallot Vinaigrette
description: A warm, homemade vinaigrette adds a tasty touch to this salad featuring non-starchy kale. It comes together quickly and makes a great appetizer or side salad for an easy weeknight meal or when you want to impress your dinner guests.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 240mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 233mg 5%
steps: In a large salad bowl, combine the chopped kale and toasted almonds.
To make the dressing: In a small saucepan, combine pitted cherries, finely chopped shallot, balsamic vinegar, and Dijon mustard.

Add the grated Parmesan cheese and garlic powder to the breadcrumbs. Stir to combine.
Toss the steamed green beans in the breadcrumb mixture until they are well-coated.
Season with the kosher salt and black pepper.
Transfer to a baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes or until the breadcrumbs are crispy and golden.

title: Grilled Green Bean Salad
description: Hot-off-the-grill green beans add a roasted, delicious flavor to this salad. Paired with a simple dressing and blue cheese, you’re sure to love this delicious side salad.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 358mg 8%
steps: Preheat the grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, toss the green beans with olive oil, garlic powder, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Place the seasoned green beans on the preheated grill. Grill for 8–10 minutes, turning occasionally, or until the beans are tender and have grill marks.
While the green beans are grilling, prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, and 2 Tbsp chopped fresh basil. Add tomatoes to the dressing.
Once the green beans are done, transfer them to a serving platter.
Pour dressing and tomatoes over the green bean salad.
Top with the crumbled blue cheese and remaining basil leaves.

title: Grilled Lime Chicken Salad Lettuce Wraps
description: Fresh, crunchy, and delicious, these Grilled Lime Chicken Salad Lettuce Wraps are an excellent lunch choice for people with diabetes.
nutrients_raw: Calories 170; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 65mg 22%; Sodium 100mg 4%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 24g; Potassium 346mg 7%
ingredients: 12 leaves lettuce leaves (large, such as butter or iceberg)
steps: In a bowl, combine the lime zest, lime juice, olive oil, minced garlic, ground cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper to make the marinade.
Place the chicken breasts in a sealable bag or shallow dish and pour half of the marinade over the chicken. Toss to fully coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the grill or a grill pan over medium high heat.
Grill the marinated chicken breasts for about 6–8 minutes per side or until fully cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degreed F.
Allow the chicken to rest for a few minutes before slicing it into strips.
In a bowl, combine cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and fresh cilantro.
Pour the remaining marinade over the vegetable mixture and toss gently.
Place two lettuce leaves on each plate.
Top with the vegetable salad mixture.

title: Grilled Zucchini Bites with Tomato, Olive, and Pinenut Salsa
description: Amp up your grilled zucchini with this diabetes-friendly recipe. A fresh salsa made of tomatoes, olives, and pine nuts adds a savory kick to low-carb zucchini.
nutrients_raw: Calories 60; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 172mg 4%
steps: In a small bowl, mix together the tomato, kalamata olives, pine nuts, parsley, and ¼ tsp kosher salt. Set aside.
Preheat a grill pan or grill over medium high heat.
In a bowl, toss zucchini slices with coconut oil, minced garlic, and ¼ tsp kosher salt. Place on grill and grill 3 minutes per side.
Serve each slice warm with a generous topping of the salsa.

title: Grilled Zucchini
description: This grilled zucchini is a quick side dish that is simple, fresh, and full of flavor.
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 3g 1%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 256mg 5%
steps: Preheat the grill or a grill pan to 350 degrees.
In a large bowl, toss the zucchini rounds with olive oil, dried thyme, salt, and pepper.
Use tongs to place the rounds on the grill.
Grill for 3–4 minutes on each side, until tender and charred in places.

title: Mashed Butternut Squash
description: Great for a fall or winter side dish, this diabetes-friendly Mashed Butternut Squash is a delicious and low-carb alternative to mashed potatoes.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 3.5g 4%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 677mg 14%
steps: Steam or boil the butternut squash cubes until the cubes are fork-tender. If steamed, remove the cooked squash from the steamer basket and pour it into a large bowl. If boiled, strain the butternut squash and then add to a large bowl.
Add the minced garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper and mash until smooth.

title: Mashed Turnips
description: Try our vibrant Mashed Turnips recipe for a low-calorie delight bursting with vitamins and antioxidants, perfect for a nutrient-packed side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 60; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 2g; Potassium 217mg 5%
steps: Add water to a large saucepan and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Add the cubed turnips and boil until tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain and then return the turnips to the pot.
Add butter, minced garlic, and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

title: Mediterranean Baked Eggplant
description: Nutrient-rich eggplant gets a Mediterranean-inspired makeover in this easy side dish recipe. Fresh tomatoes, crumbled feta, and herbs take this diabetes-friendly dish to the next level of deliciousness.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 11g 4%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 421mg 9%
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Lay the eggplant rounds on a baking sheet.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, dried thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper.
Brush both sides of each eggplant round with the olive oil mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, then flip the eggplant rounds and bake for an additional 15 minutes or until they are tender and golden brown.
Remove the eggplant from the oven.
Sprinkle halved cherry tomatoes and crumbled feta cheese over the baked eggplant.
Return the baking sheet to the oven and bake for an additional 5 minutes, or until the feta is softened and tomatoes are slightly roasted.

title: Baked Egg and Zoodle Bundle
description: These baked zoodle bundles are a fresh, veggie-forward way to enjoy eggs with a burst of pesto flavor and creamy Greek yogurt. The higher protein and fiber content can help support steady energy throughout the morning.
nutrients_raw: Calories 140; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 190mg 63%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 361mg 8%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Lightly coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
In a small bowl, mix yogurt and pesto.
Toss the zucchini noodles with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
On the prepared baking sheet, create 4 small nests with zucchini. Evenly distribute tomato halves among them.
Bake for 5 minutes until slightly softened. Remove from the oven. Create a small well in the center of each nest. Spoon pesto yogurt mixture into each well. Crack 1 egg into each well.
Return to the oven and bake for 10-12 minutes, until eggs reach desired doneness.
Remove from the oven, sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese and fresh basil. Serve immediately.

title: Cheesy Broccoli Spaghetti Squash Bake
description: This cheesy broccoli spaghetti squash bake is a comforting, lower-carb alternative to traditional casseroles, with plenty of fiber and flavor packed into every bite.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 430mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 26g 9%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 9g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 11g; Potassium 528mg 11%
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Cut squash in half lengthwise and scoop out seeds. Drizzle with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet and roast until fork-tender, about 35-40 minutes. Let cool slightly, then use a fork to shred into strands.
While squash is roasting, bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add broccoli and cook until just tender, about 3 minutes. Drain and set aside.
In a large skillet over medium heat, add a drizzle of olive oil and cook garlic until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in broth, milk, Dijon mustard, and paprika. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and stir in cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
To prevent curdling, remove sauce from heat before adding Greek yogurt. Temper by mixing 1-2 Tbsp of warm sauce into the yogurt first, then slowly stir into the pan.

In a large mixing bowl, combine spaghetti squash, broccoli, and cheese sauce. Transfer to a baking dish and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Bake at 400°F for 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and slightly golden.

title: Cheesy Tomato and White Bean "Pizza" Skillet
description: This “pizza” skillet combines the comfort of a cheesy tomato bake with the wholesomeness of white beans and spinach for a satisfying one-pan meal. It’s rich in plant-based protein and fiber, which can help promote stable blood sugar (blood glucose) levels.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 5g 6%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 25g 9%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 12g; Potassium 720mg 15%
ingredients: 1 1/2 cup canned crushed tomatoes (no added salt)
1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans (no added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to broil.

Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in the garlic, oregano, and red pepper flakes, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth, then season with the salt and black pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the white beans and spinach, cooking for another 3-4 minutes until the spinach wilts and the beans are heated through.
Sprinkle the mozzarella and Parmesan evenly over the skillet. Place the skillet in the oven and broil until the cheese is melted and golden-brown, 2-3 minutes.
Remove from the oven and garnish with fresh basil.

title: Chickpea Salad with Creamy Tahini Dressing
description: This crisp and refreshing chickpea salad is tossed with a creamy homemade tahini dressing for a simple, plant-based meal that’s big on flavor and fiber. Chickpeas provide satisfying protein and slow-digesting carbs that can help support stable blood glucose (blood sugar). It’s a nourishing, no-cook option that’s especially well-suited for those looking for a fresh, filling lunch.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 10g 36%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 10g; Potassium 640mg 14%
ingredients: 1 cup canned chickpeas (no added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a medium bowl, combine the tahini, fresh lemon juice, crushed garlic, and salt.​ Gradually add cold water, whisking continuously until the dressing reaches a smooth, pourable consistency.​
In a separate large bowl, combine the chopped romaine lettuce, cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, and chickpeas.​ Add sliced red onion and chopped parsley. Drizzle the tahini dressing over the salad.​

title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken with Spinach
description: This Tuscan chicken has creamy comfort without the heavy cream, thanks to a mix of low-fat milk and Greek yogurt. With lean protein, fiber-rich spinach, and no added sugars, it’s a balanced dish that will help you reach your blood glucose (blood sugar) goals. It’s a great choice if you’re looking for something hearty, flavorful, and diabetes friendly.
nutrients_raw: Calories 230; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 90mg 30%; Sodium 400mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 32g; Potassium 599mg 13%
ingredients: 12 oz low sodium chicken broth (fat free)
1/2 cup fresh basil (torn, plus more for serving)
steps: Sprinkle the chicken breasts with the pepper, garlic powder, and oregano. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken and sear until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 4–5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.

In the same skillet, add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Pour in the chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in the milk, sun-dried tomatoes, and red pepper flakes. Simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and Parmesan cheese, cooking until spinach wilts, about 1–2 minutes.

Remove the pan from the heat once the sauce is finished simmering. In a small bowl, mix ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt with 1–2 Tbsp of the warm sauce to temper it. Slowly stir the tempered yogurt into the pan, mixing gently until fully incorporated.
Return the chicken to the pan. Spoon the sauce over the top. Add half of the basil and simmer for 1–2 minutes to heat through.
Serve with additional fresh basil on top.

title: Melon with Tarragon Vinaigrette
description: Melon with Tarragon Vinaigrette is a refreshing and elegant salad that combines the sweetness of ripe melon with the herby and slightly peppery notes of tarragon in a light vinaigrette. It makes for a great low-carb side dish in the summer.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 170mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 11g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 275mg 6%
steps: In a small bowl, whisk lemon juice, syrup, chopped tarragon, and oil.
Arrange cantaloupe on a platter, drizzle generously with dressing, and finish with a sprinkling of salt.

title: Low Carb Sushi Bowl
description: This low-carb sushi bowl is a fresh take on takeout, swapping traditional rice for seasoned cauliflower to keep the carbs down without losing flavor. Shrimp adds lean protein, while avocado and veggies bring satisfying texture and healthy fats. It’s a diabetes-friendly option that supports blood glucose (blood sugar) levels without sacrificing any flavor.
serving_size: 3 oz cauliflower rice + 2 oz shrimp + 1 cup veggies + 1 Tbsp mayo
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 95mg 32%; Sodium 390mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 16g; Potassium 426mg 9%
steps: Cook the frozen cauliflower rice according to package instructions. Transfer to a bowl and mix in the vinegar, sesame oil, and salt. Let it cool to room temp.
In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, sriracha, and lime juice. Set aside.
To assemble, divide the cauliflower rice among 4 bowls. Top each bowl with the diced shrimp, avocado, cucumber, radishes, and green onions.
Drizzle the spicy mayo over each bowl and top with sesame seeds.

title: Philly Cheesesteak Stuffed Peppers
description: These Philly Cheesesteak-Stuffed Peppers have all the savory flavors of the original—but without the roll. Swapping the bread for bell peppers helps cut back on carbs while adding fiber and nutrients. It's a great lower carb dinner that can help support steady blood glucose (blood sugar).
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 50mg 17%; Sodium 270mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 22g; Potassium 594mg 13%
ingredients: 2 whole green bell pepper (halved lengthwise, seeds removed)
12 oz top round steak (trimmed of fat, thinly sliced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Arrange the bell pepper halves on a baking sheet with the cut sides facing up. Bake for about 30 minutes or until they are tender but still firm enough to hold their shape.

While the peppers are in the oven, warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and cook for about 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they soften and start to brown.
Stir in the mushrooms and continue cooking for another 5 minutes, allowing them to release their moisture.
Add the steak slices to the pan, along with the Italian seasoning, black pepper, and salt. Cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the steak is browned and cooked through.
Pour in the Worcestershire sauce, stir to combine, and remove the skillet from the heat.
Switch the oven to broil.
Fill each bell pepper half with an equal portion of the steak mixture and sprinkle with cheese.
Return the peppers to the oven and broil for 2–3 minutes, or until the cheese is fully melted and slightly golden.
Top with the chopped green onion to serve.

title: Rotini Caesar Salad with Garlic Croutons
description: This lighter take on Caesar salad blends creamy Greek yogurt dressing with whole grain pasta and crisp romaine for a satisfying, fiber-rich dish. Homemade garlic croutons and shaved Parmesan add crunch and flavor. With smart ingredient swaps and portioned pasta, it’s a balanced, diabetes-friendly spin on a classic favorite.
serving_size: 1 oz pasta + 1/4 cup croutons + 2 cup salad
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 36g 13%; Dietary Fiber 7g 25%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 14g; Potassium 601mg 13%
ingredients: 2 slice whole grain Ezekiel 4:9 bread (cut into small cubes)
4 oz roasted red peppers (sliced into strips)
4 oz whole wheat penne pasta (cooked and cooled)
steps: Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the bread cubes, then sprinkle with dried oregano and garlic powder. Toast the cubes, stirring frequently, until they are golden brown and crisp, about 4-5 minutes. Remove from the skillet and let them cool.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, 2 tsp olive oil, and black pepper until smooth and well combined.
In a large bowl, toss the chopped romaine lettuce and peppers with the dressing, ensuring everything is evenly coated.
Gently mix the cooked pasta into the salad. Add the toasted croutons and toss lightly to combine.
Divide into 4 servings and top with shaved Parmesan cheese.

title: Smoked Salmon and Greek Yogurt Omelet
description: This elegant omelet pairs silky smoked salmon with creamy Greek yogurt and fresh dill for a protein-rich, satisfying start to the day. It’s a smart breakfast option for those watching their blood glucose (blood sugar), thanks to its low carbohydrate content and balanced protein.
nutrients_raw: Calories 160; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 210mg 70%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 2g <1%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 20g; Potassium 242mg 5%
ingredients: 2 oz cold smoked salmon (low sodium, chopped)
1 tbsp fresh dill (chopped, plus more for garnish)
steps: In a bowl, whisk the eggs, egg whites, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Pour ¼ of the egg mixture into the skillet, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook until the edges start to set, about 2 minutes.
Add ¼ of the smoked salmon, a dollop of Greek yogurt, fresh dill, and red onion to one side of the omelet.
Carefully fold the omelet over the filling and cook for 30 seconds to warm through.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining ingredients.

title: Smoky Beef Burger on a Mushroom Bun
description: This burger stacks smoky beef, melted cheddar, and grilled veggies on a savory portobello mushroom “bun” for a low-carb alternative to the classic. Grated zucchini keeps the patties juicy while adding a sneaky dose of veggies.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 60mg 20%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 31g; Potassium 961mg 20%
ingredients: 1 small zucchini (grated, squeezed to remove excess moisture)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, smoked paprika, grated zucchini, and 1 tablespoon of the barbecue sauce. Mix thoroughly using clean hands, then shape the mixture into four patties, each about ¾-inch thick.

Preheat a large grill pan over medium-high heat. Lightly brush the patties and portobello mushrooms with olive oil. Place the mushrooms on the grill and cook for 4-5 minutes on each side until they are tender and have light char marks.

Cook the beef patties for about 4 minutes on the first side until lightly charred. Flip the patties, cook for an additional 2 minutes, then top each with a slice of cheddar cheese. Continue cooking for another 2 minutes until the cheese melts and the patties are cooked through.
Grill the red onion rings for about 2 minutes on each side until they are lightly charred.

To serve, place each grilled mushroom cap on a plate, gill side up. Top with arugula, a slice of tomato, a beef patty with melted cheese, and some grilled onion rings. Drizzle with the remaining barbecue sauce.

title: Southwest Shredded Pork Salad
description: This Southwest-inspired salad layers tender shredded pork with crisp greens, colorful veggies, and a tangy Greek yogurt dressing. It’s high in protein and fiber, with smart seasoning swaps.
nutrients_raw: Calories 250; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 75mg 25%; Sodium 440mg 19%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 30g; Potassium 940mg 20%
ingredients: 1/2 cup black beans (canned, low sodium, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a small bowl, combine the cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, onion powder, and 1/4 tsp pepper. Rub this spice mixture evenly over the pork tenderloin.​
Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork and sear on all sides until browned, about 2-3 minutes per side.​
Transfer the pork to a slow cooker and add the low-sodium chicken broth. Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours, or until the pork is tender and shreds easily with a fork.​
Once cooked, remove the pork from the slow cooker and shred it using two forks. Set aside.​

In a small bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, lime juice, remaining 2 tsp olive oil, remaining 1/4 tsp chili powder, remaining 1/4 tsp garlic powder, salt, and remaining 1/8 tsp pepper until smooth.
Divide the mixed salad greens among four plates or bowls.​
Top each with equal portions of cherry tomatoes, cucumber, black beans, corn, and red onion.​
Add a portion of the shredded pork to each salad.​
Drizzle the dressing over each salad and gently toss to combine.​ Garnish with fresh cilantro.

title: Orange and Avocado Salad
description: Bright orange and creamy avocado come together in this unique, diabetes-friendly salad. Perfect as a side dish, pair it with a lean protein like grilled chicken breasts for a quick and easy meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 200; Total Fat 14g 18%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 125mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 19g 7%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 439mg 9%
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together extra-virgin olive oil, lime juice, unsweetened multi-use syrup, salt, and black pepper.
Arrange oranges, avocados, red onion, and fresh mint on a platter.
Pour the dressing over the salad and top with toasted slivered almonds.

title: Miso Chopped Salad
description: The crunch of cabbage, carrots, and onion pair with an Asian infusion dressing that is diabetes-friendly and would go great with a stir fry dinner!
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 370mg 16%; Total Carbohydrate 16g 6%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 3g; Potassium 338mg 7%
ingredients: 2 stalks scallions (chopped, white and light green parts)
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the soy sauce, white rice miso paste, rice wine vinegar, toasted sesame oil, olive oil, unsweetened multi-use syrup, fresh ginger, and lime juice in a small bowl.
Add in the cabbage, red onion, corn, carrot, scallions, and cilantro and toss to combine.
Allow to rest at least 15 minutes before serving so flavors can meld.

title: Parmesan Roasted Cauliflower
description: Upgrade your roasted cauliflower with some creamy parmesan cheese. This Italian-inspired recipe is a great low carb option to add to your dinner.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 280mg 12%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 434mg 9%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
In a large bowl, toss cauliflower florets with olive oil, grated Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper until well coated.
Spread the cauliflower in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25 minutes or until the cauliflower is golden brown and crispy, tossing halfway through.
Remove the cauliflower from the oven.
Transfer the cauliflower to a serving dish.
Serve the cauliflower as a savory and diabetes-friendly side dish.

title: Perfect Sautéed Carrots
description: It may be bold, but we think these are the perfect way to sauté carrots! Slightly caramelizing the carrots adds a delectable richness and sweetness to this simple recipe and is sure to be a hit with the whole family.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 380mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 364mg 8%
ingredients: 1 lbs carrots (peeled and cut into 2–3-inch sticks)
steps: In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add the carrots to the skillet, spreading them out in a single layer.
Sauté the carrots for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Season the carrots with the salt, thyme and black pepper.

title: Quick and Easy Sautéed Collard Greens
description: Experience the swift and effortless preparation of sautéed collard greens, where vibrant greens are delicately cooked to perfection, offering a quick and easy side dish that's both nutritious and flavorful.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 160mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 187mg 4%
ingredients: 1 bunch collard greens (stems removed and leaves chopped)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes, if using, to the skillet. Sauté for 1–2 minutes until the garlic becomes fragrant.
Add the collard greens to the skillet. Toss to coat in the garlic and oil.
Sauté the collard greens for 5–7 minutes, or until they are wilted and tender.
Season with the salt and black pepper.
Drizzle apple cider vinegar over the collard greens. Toss to combine.
Continue cooking for an additional 2–3 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

title: Roasted Asparagus and Tomatoes
description: This delightful recipe is all about the simplicity of roasted asparagus and tomatoes, where the tender crunch of asparagus meets the burst of sweetness from roasted tomatoes, creating a diabetes-friendly, vitamin-rich medley.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 150mg 7%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 336mg 7%
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F and cover a sheet pan in parchment paper.
Toss asparagus and cherry tomatoes with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Spread evenly on the sheet pan and roast for 15–20 minutes until asparagus is tender and tomatoes are slightly caramelized.
Platter and garnish with fresh basil.

title: Roasted Beets with Blue Cheese and Hazelnuts
description: This gourmet dish not only showcases vibrant colors, but also adds a sophisticated touch to your diabetes-conscious dining, creating a delightful balance of textures and tastes in every delectable bite.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 340mg 7%
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish, optional)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, toss the diced beets with olive oil, salt, and black pepper until well coated.
Spread the beets in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 45 minutes or until the beets are tender, stirring halfway through.
Remove the beets from the oven and transfer them to a serving dish.
Sprinkle crumbled blue cheese and toasted hazelnuts over the roasted beets.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

title: Roasted Broccolini with Lemon and Parmesan
description: Experience the perfect balance of flavors in our roasted broccolini with zesty lemon and parmesan in this diabetes-friendly side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 9g 12%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 6g; Potassium 357mg 8%
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Zest and juice one lemon.

In a large bowl, toss broccolini with olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, grated Parmesan cheese, minced garlic, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Ensure the broccolini is evenly coated.
Spread the broccolini in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 15 minutes or until the broccolini is tender-crisp and the edges are slightly charred.
Serve with additional grated Parmesan on top. Slice the remaining lemon into wedges to serve on the side if desired.

title: Roasted Carrots with Crispy Bacon
description: If you consider yourself a bacon aficionado, then you’ll love these roasted carrots with crispy bacon. The unexpected pairing adds a touch of fun to this diabetes-friendly side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 100; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 5mg 2%; Sodium 260mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 277mg 6%
ingredients: 4 slice bacon (cooked until crispy and crumbled)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, toss the carrot sticks with the olive oil until they are well-coated.
Spread the carrots in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Sprinkle the salt and black pepper over the carrots.
Roast in the preheated oven for 20–25 minutes or until the carrots are tender and slightly caramelized, stirring them halfway through.
Remove the carrots from the oven. Transfer them to a serving dish.
Sprinkle the crispy bacon over the roasted carrots. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

title: Chicken Cobb Salad with Turkey Bacon
description: This chicken Cobb salad is packed with lean protein, fresh vegetables, and heart-healthy fats. It comes together quickly, making it a great addition to your lunch rotation.
serving_size: 3 oz chicken + 3 cups salad + 2 Tbsp dressing
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 75mg 25%; Sodium 420mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 8g 3%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 30g; Potassium 504mg 11%
ingredients: 1-2 tbsp water (as needed for desired consistency)
4 slice turkey bacon (low sodium, cooked and crumbled)
steps: Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the diced chicken breast, paprika, ⅛ tsp salt, and pepper. Sauté until the chicken is fully cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degrees F and golden brown. Remove from the heat and set aside.

To make the dressing, combine the Greek yogurt, dill, chives, parsley, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, rice vinegar, water, and remaining ¼ tsp salt, in a blender or food processor and pulse until smooth.
Divide the lettuce between 4 bowls. Top with the chicken, bacon, tomatoes, avocado, and egg whites. Drizzle with the dressing.

title: Turkish Eggs with Herbed Greek Yogurt
description: This twist on Turkish eggs layers creamy herbed Greek yogurt with perfectly poached eggs and a fragrant spiced olive oil drizzle. The combination of protein-rich yogurt and eggs makes for a filling, blood glucose (blood sugar)-friendly breakfast. Served with sprouted grain bread or on its own, it’s a flavorful option for those looking to balance carbs without sacrificing taste.
nutrients_raw: Calories 180; Total Fat 10g 13%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 195mg 65%; Sodium 400mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 0g 0%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 17g; Potassium 150mg 3%
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh herbs (chopped, such as dill or parsley, plus extra for garnish)
steps: In a medium bowl, mix the Greek yogurt, garlic, fresh herbs, and lemon zest. Season with ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Set aside at room temperature.
Make the spiced oil. In a small pan over low heat, warm olive oil with paprika, cumin, and red pepper flakes. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Remove from heat and set aside.

Fill a medium saucepan with 2-3 inches of water and bring to a gentle simmer. Add vinegar. Crack eggs into small bowls. Swirl the water, then gently slide in the eggs. Cook for 3-4 minutes until whites are set but yolks remain runny. Use a slotted spoon to transfer eggs to a paper towel-lined plate.
Divide the Greek yogurt mixture between bowls. Top with poached eggs and drizzle with spiced olive oil. Garnish with extra fresh herbs and remaining ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper.
Pair each serving with 1/2 slice of sprouted whole grain bread.

title: Cauliflower Rice and Beans Fajita Bowls
description: In this diabetes-friendly and vegan meal, beans add some delicious plant-based protein to your meal. Making rice out of cauliflower is a great way to get more nutrients in your diet without adding extra carbs. Top your bowl with some fresh cilantro or salsa for a little extra kick.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 460mg 20%; Total Carbohydrate 36g 13%; Dietary Fiber 13g 46%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 12g; Potassium 1159mg 25%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans (no added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a food processor, pulse the cauliflower until it resembles rice. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add sliced bell peppers and red onion. Sauté until the vegetables are tender, about 5–7 minutes.
Add the riced cauliflower to the skillet. Sprinkle the ground cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, kosher salt, and black pepper. Stir well to combine.
Cook the cauliflower mixture for an additional 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cauliflower is tender.
Stir in the black beans and cook for an additional 3–5 minutes until everything is heated through.
Squeeze lime juice over the mixture and stir.
Divide the cauliflower rice and beans fajita mixture into bowls. Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh cilantro if desired.

title: Roasted Pepper and Caper Salad
description: This Italian inspired salad is a great way to add some non-starchy vegetables to your plate. Lower in carbs, but high in taste, your whole family with enjoy this fresh and healthy choice.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 11g 14%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 310mg 13%; Total Carbohydrate 9g 3%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 1g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 1g; Potassium 273mg 6%
steps: Preheat the oven broiler. Place the whole bell peppers on a baking sheet and broil, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and blistered. Remove from the oven and let them cool. Once cool, peel off the skin, remove seeds, and slice into strips.
In a bowl, combine the roasted pepper strips, drained capers, sliced Kalamata olives, and chopped fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together extra-virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the roasted pepper mixture. Toss gently to combine, ensuring even coating.
Let the salad marinate for at least 15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

title: Roasted Delicata Squash with Pomegranate Glaze
description: Indulge in the exquisite fusion of flavors with our roasted delicata squash, featuring a luscious pomegranate glaze that transforms each bite into a sweet and savory side you’ll want to enjoy again and again.
nutrients_raw: Calories 130; Total Fat 4.5g 6%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 190mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 10g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 3g; Potassium 821mg 17%
ingredients: 2 whole delicata squash (halved, seeded, and sliced into half-moons (3 lb total))
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
In a bowl, toss the delicata squash slices with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, pomegranate molasses, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Spread the squash slices in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Roast in the preheated oven for about 20–25 minutes or until the squash is tender and caramelized, flipping the slices halfway through.
Remove from the oven and transfer to a serving dish.
Drizzle any remaining glaze from the baking sheet over the squash.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds for a burst of freshness and color.
Serve as a flavorful and visually appealing side dish.

title: Roasted Garlic Cauliflower Mash
description: This creamy delight not only can sub in for a low-carb alternative to garlic mashed potatoes, but you might also find you like it even better!
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 4g 5%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 140mg 6%; Total Carbohydrate 12g 4%; Dietary Fiber 5g 18%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 670mg 14%
ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh herbs (Chopped, for garnish, such as dill or parsley)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the cauliflower florets and unpeeled garlic cloves on a baking sheet.
Drizzle the olive oil over the cauliflower and garlic. Toss to coat evenly.
Sprinkle with the salt and black pepper.
Roast in the preheated oven for 25–30 minutes or until the cauliflower is tender and golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly.
Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves out of their skins.
In a food processor, combine the roasted cauliflower, roasted garlic, almond milk, and nutritional yeast.
Blend until smooth and creamy. If needed, add more almond milk for desired consistency.
Garnish with fresh chopped herbs if desired.

title: Roasted Green Beans with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
description: Similar to green bean casserole, these tender roasted green beans pair delightfully with a homemade creamy mushroom sauce in this diabetes-friendly side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 110; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 200mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 2g 7%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 288mg 6%
ingredients: 1 lbs fresh green beans (fresh, ends trimmed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
Toss the trimmed green beans with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the green beans in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for 20 minutes or until the green beans are tender-crisp and slightly caramelized, tossing halfway through.
While the green beans are roasting, prepare the mushroom sauce.
For the creamy mushroom sauce: In a skillet, heat 2 Tbsp olive oil over medium heat.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the skillet and sauté until they release their moisture and become golden brown.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and stir continuously for 1–2 minutes to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in vegetable broth and milk to the skillet, ensuring no lumps form.
Add minced garlic, salt, and black pepper. Stir continuously until the sauce thickens.
Reduce the heat and let the sauce simmer for an additional 2–3 minutes.
Remove the sauce from the heat.
To finish, once the green beans are roasted, transfer them to a serving dish and spoon the creamy mushroom sauce over the top.

title: Roasted Green Beans with Lemon and Sesame

title: Sautéed Cabbage with Cider Vinegar Dressing
description: Sautéed cabbage adorned in a cider vinegar dressing, where the gentle crispness of cabbage meets the tangy allure of a flavorful dressing. This diabetes-friendly dish is easy enough for a weeknight meal.

steps: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the thinly sliced cabbage to the skillet, tossing to coat in the oil.
Sauté the cabbage for 10–12 minutes or until it is tender but still has a bit of crunch.
In a small bowl, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, and caraway seeds.
Pour the cider vinegar dressing over the sautéed cabbage. Toss to coat evenly.

title: Sautéed Cabbage with Lemon Butter

steps: Add the olive oil to a large skillet and heat on medium-high.
Sauté the shredded cabbage until tender but still crisp, about 3–5 minutes.

In a small saucepan, melt the butter and stir in the water, lemon zest, lemon juice, and poppy seeds.

Add kale and cook until darkened and tender, about 5 minutes.

title: Sautéed Kale with Crispy Bacon and Shallots
description: This modern take on nutrient-rich sautéed kale adds smoky and crunchy bacon and shallots. Add a kick of spice with red pepper flakes if you want to amp up the flavor profile of this side dish.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 210mg 9%; Total Carbohydrate 5g 2%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 4g; Potassium 190mg 4%
ingredients: 1 bunch kale (stems removed and leaves chopped)
steps: In a large skillet, cook the chopped bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove the bacon from the skillet and place it on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess fat. Wipe out skillet.
In the same skillet, add olive oil over medium heat.
Add the thinly sliced shallots to the skillet and sauté for 2–3 minutes until they start to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and sauté for an additional 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chopped kale to the skillet in batches, allowing each batch to wilt before adding more.
Once all the kale is in the skillet, pour apple cider vinegar over the greens.
Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Toss to combine.
Continue sautéing for 5–7 minutes or until the kale is tender but still vibrant.
Transfer the kale to a serving dish and sprinkle the crispy bacon on top.

title: Sautéed Spinach
description: It’s never been so easy to add some green, non-starchy veggies to your plate with this simple sautéed spinach. Ready to go in minutes, it’s a great diabetes-friendly option for weeknight meals.
nutrients_raw: Calories 90; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 230mg 10%; Total Carbohydrate 4g 1%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 0g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 3g; Potassium 6mg <1%
ingredients: 1 lbs frozen spinach (washed and stems removed)
steps: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the garlic to the skillet and sauté for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the fresh spinach to the skillet in batches, allowing each batch to wilt before adding more.
Toss the spinach gently to coat it with the olive oil and garlic.
Continue sautéing for 2–3 minutes or until the spinach is wilted and tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Toss to combine.
Serve with lemon wedges on the side if desired.

title: Sesame Broccoli with Scallions
description: This Sesame Broccoli with Scallions is a quick and tasty side dish that brings out the natural crispiness of broccoli, with an Asian flair using sesame and scallions. A perfect, diabetes-friendly addition to your meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 120; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 400mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 2g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 5g; Potassium 437mg 9%
ingredients: 2 stalks scallions (Thinly sliced, white and green parts)
steps: In a large pot, bring water to a boil. Add the broccoli florets and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain and transfer the broccoli to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking process. Drain again.
In a large skillet or wok, heat the sesame oil over medium-high heat.
Add the blanched broccoli to the skillet. Stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until the broccoli is tender-crisp.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce and rice vinegar.
Pour the soy sauce mixture over the broccoli. Toss to coat evenly.
Continue cooking for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
Remove the broccoli from the heat.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallions over the broccoli. Toss gently.

title: Shaved Brussels Sprouts with Candied Bacon and Cranberries
description: If you didn’t like Brussels sprouts as a kid, it’s time to give them another try with this delicious salad. With enough protein and greens to keep you satisfied, this salad is a full meal all in one dish!
nutrients_raw: Calories 190; Total Fat 12g 15%; Saturated Fat 2g 10%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 10mg 3%; Sodium 110mg 5%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 6g 21%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 8g; Potassium 569mg 12%
ingredients: 1 lbs brussels sprouts (trimmed and thinly sliced)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, combine the brown sugar substitute, 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Lay the bacon slices on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer, ensuring they do not overlap.
Sprinkle the brown sugar mixture evenly over each bacon slice, pressing it gently to adhere.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven and transfer the candied bacon to a plate lined with paper towels to absorb excess grease. Let cool for a few minutes.
In a large bowl, place the thinly sliced Brussels sprouts. Add the candied bacon, dried cranberries, and toasted sliced almonds.
In a smaller bowl, whisk together the balsamic vinegar, olive oil, salt, and remaining pepper to create the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the Brussels sprouts mixture.
Toss the salad gently to ensure even coating.

title: Smashed Spicy Broccoli

steps: Steam the broccoli florets until they are just tender, about 5 minutes. Alternatively, blanch them in boiling water for 3–4 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Sprinkle the crispy garlic and sesame seeds over the steamed broccoli.

ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and diced into bite-sized cubes)

Roast in the preheated oven for 30 minutes or until the sweet potatoes are tender and slightly caramelized, stirring halfway through.

Spoon chimichurri sauce generously over each cauliflower steak.

title: Cheesy Sweet Potato and Black Bean Casserole
description: Try this Cheesy Sweet Potato and Black Bean Casserole, a flavorful and hearty dish that brings together the rich sweetness of sweet potatoes, the earthy goodness of black beans, and the gooey comfort of melted cheese. Best of all? This recipe is diabetes-friendly!

ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and thinly sliced)

title: Pasta Fagioli (Italian Pasta and Beans)

Gradually pour in vegetable broth, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Add dried thyme, pepper, and frozen peas. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.

Top filling with biscuits.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10–15 minutes until biscuits are golden brown. Cut into 4 pieces and serve.

ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans black beans (low sodium, drained and rinsed)

steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Toss the halved Brussels sprouts with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread the Brussels sprouts in a single layer on a baking sheet.

ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh dill (finely chopped, plus more for garnish)

Garnish with more dill.

ingredients: 1 head lettuce (such as red oak, green leaf or romaine)

Add the chicken and any remaining marinade to the hot pan. Cook, stirring frequently, until most of the liquid has evaporated and the chicken is browned, about 10 minutes. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Kung Pao Chicken and Vegetables

ingredients: 1-inch piece fresh ginger (peeled, quartered, and smashed)

steps: Whisk together the rice vinegar, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, honey, and cornstarch in a small bowl. Whisk until the cornstarch has dissolved and the sauce is smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add the ginger, garlic, and chili-garlic sauce and sauté until fragrant, about 15 seconds.

Stir in the bell peppers and cook until slightly softened, about 2 minutes.

Pour egg substitute into the well, season with salt and pepper, and scramble until cooked through.
Once the eggs are almost set, mix them with the turkey and vegetables.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the scramble and cover the skillet until the cheese melts.

In a separate skillet, warm the rice and black beans together.

title: Apple Cider Muffins
description: These apple cider muffins offer a diabetes-friendly twist on a fall classic that tastes delicious any time of year.
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 30mg 10%; Sodium 190mg 8%; Total Carbohydrate 23g 8%; Dietary Fiber 3g 11%; Total Sugars 6g; Added Sugars 2g 4%; Protein 4g; Potassium 53mg 1%
steps: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F. Lightly coat 2 standard-sized muffin pans with nonstick cooking spray.
Boil the apple cider in a saucepan over medium heat until it's reduced by half, leaving about 3/4 cup. Set aside to cool.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, 1 tsp of the ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, and salt.
In a separate bowl, mix the unsweetened applesauce, sugar substitute, eggs, apple cider, avocado oil, and vanilla extract together.
Gradually stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined. Do not overmix. Spoon the batter into each cavity, filling about two-thirds full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 18 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.
In a small bowl, stir together the granulated sugar and ½ tsp of ground cinnamon to create the cinnamon sugar.
While the muffins are cooling in the pan, lightly dust the cinnamon sugar over the tops.
Let the dusted muffins cool in the pan before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Baked Spiced Sweet Potato Fries with Low Fat Yogurt Dipping Sauce
description: Deliciously spiced, these aren’t your typical sweet potato fries. Served with a tangy and creamy dipping sauce, this side is one you’ll want to make all year long.
serving_size: ½ cup sweet potato fries + 2 Tbsp dipping sauce
nutrients_raw: Calories 80; Total Fat 2.5g 3%; Saturated Fat 0.5g 3%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 250mg 11%; Total Carbohydrate 10g 4%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 3g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 3g; Potassium 178mg 4%
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (peeled and cut into fries)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato fries with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Arrange the seasoned sweet potato fries in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, ensuring they are not crowded.
Lightly spray the fries with cooking spray for extra crispiness.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20–25 minutes or until the sweet potato fries are golden brown and crispy, flipping them halfway through.
For the dipping sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the low-fat Greek yogurt, lemon juice, maple syrup, and ground cumin.
Serve dipping sauce on the side.

title: High Protein Banana Pancakes
description: Greek yogurt adds extra protein to these diabetes-friendly banana pancakes. Hearty oats and a dash of cinnamon add depth of flavor for a breakfast that will keep you powered through your morning.
nutrients_raw: Calories 240; Total Fat 6g 8%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 145mg 48%; Sodium 330mg 14%; Total Carbohydrate 27g 10%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 7g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 20g; Potassium 380mg 8%
steps: In a blender or food processor, combine the oats, protein powder, banana, eggs, Greek yogurt, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla extract, and salt. Blend until smooth.
Let the batter sit for a few minutes to thicken slightly.
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat and lightly spray with cooking spray.
Pour 1/4 cup portions of batter onto the skillet to form small pancakes.
Cook for 2–3 minutes on one side or until bubbles form on the surface.
Flip the pancakes and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until golden brown.
Repeat until all the batter is used.

title: Mushroom and Spinach Omelet
description: Kickstart your day with a low-carb, protein-rich Mushroom and Spinach Omelet—a diabetes-friendly breakfast that turns the ordinary into the extraordinary. Picture a fluffy omelet embracing a hearty filling of sautéed mushrooms and fresh spinach with just a touch of melted cheese.
nutrients_raw: Calories 150; Total Fat 8g 10%; Saturated Fat 1.5g 8%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 0mg 0%; Sodium 400mg 17%; Total Carbohydrate 7g 3%; Dietary Fiber 1g 4%; Total Sugars 4g; Added Sugars 0g 0%; Protein 14g; Potassium 543mg 12%
steps: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet and sauté for 5–6 minutes or until the onion becomes translucent.

Add the sliced mushrooms to the skillet and cook for about 5–7 minutes until they become tender and any moisture evaporates. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the mushroom mixture from the skillet and set it aside.
Using the same skillet, lightly coat it with cooking spray and place it over medium-low heat. Pour half the egg substitute into the skillet, swirling to create an even layer.
Allow the eggs to cook undisturbed for a few minutes until they start to set. Then, using a spatula, lift the edges of the omelet and tilt the pan to let any uncooked eggs flow to the edges.

Once the omelet is mostly set but is still slightly runny on top, add half the sautéed mushroom mixture and half the chopped spinach on one side of the omelet. Sprinkle 1 tbsp low-fat grated cheese on top of the vegetables.
Carefully fold the other half of the omelet over the filling to create a half-moon shape. Cook for another 1–2 minutes until the omelet is cooked through, but not overcooked.
Gently slide the omelet onto a plate and repeat the process to make the second omelet.

title: Turkey Gumbo
description: Gumbo is a traditional Louisiana dish with a rich and thick broth. This diabetes-friendly recipe uses turkey as a lean protein and a variety of spices to make a flavorful meal.
nutrients_raw: Calories 260; Total Fat 7g 9%; Saturated Fat 1g 5%; Trans Fats 0g; Cholesterol 40mg 13%; Sodium 410mg 18%; Total Carbohydrate 28g 10%; Dietary Fiber 4g 14%; Total Sugars 5g; Added Sugars 1g 2%; Protein 22g; Potassium 560mg 12%
steps: In a large pot or Dutch oven, brown the ground turkey over medium-high heat until cooked through. Transfer the cooked turkey to a separate bowl and set aside.
In the same pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion, green bell pepper, celery, okra, and garlic, then cook until vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the Cajun seasoning, thyme, oregano, cayenne pepper, salt, pepper, and flour over the vegetables. Stir well to coat.
Gradually pour in the chicken broth, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Add the cooked turkey back to the pot, along with diced tomatoes. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and let it cook for 20–30 minutes, until the flavors meld together.
Serve the Turkey Gumbo over cooked brown rice and garnish with green onions.

title: Pollo con Glaseado de Albaricoque
description: ¡Te presentamos una nueva forma de disfrutar de los albaricoques frescos para la cena de esta primavera! Sirve este pollo con un grano integral de tu elección y una ensalada de rúcula como acompañamiento para una comida completa de temporada.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 190; Grasa Total 5g 6%; Grasa Saturada 1g 5%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 65mg 22%; Sodio 60mg 3%; Carbohidratos Totales 17g 6%; Fibra dietética 1g 4%; Azúcares totales 6g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 23g; Potasio 300mg 6%
ingredients: 1/2 taza conservas de albaricoque sin azúcar añadido (sugar-free)
4 albaricoques (fresh, pitted and cut into quarters)
1 lbs pechugas de pollo deshuesadas y sin piel (cut into 4 oz portions)
steps: Precalienta el horno a 350°F (177°C). En una sartén grande, calienta 2 cditas. de aceite a fuego medio. Añadir los albaricoques, córtalos hacia abajo y cocina hasta que estén ligeramente dorados, aproximadamente 3 minutos. Voltea los albaricoques y cocina por 1 minuto más. Reserva.

En una cacerola pequeña, añade las conservas de albaricoque, el vinagre balsámico y la pimienta y lleva a ebullición baja; cocina a fuego lento por 3 minutos o hasta que la mezcla tenga una consistencia similar a un glaseado. Añadir los albaricoques a la mezcla.

Cubre un molde para hornear con aceite en aerosol. Coloca las pechugas de pollo en un plato. Unta cada pechuga con 1 cda de glaseado de albaricoque y hornea por 30 minutos. Vierte el glaseado restante sobre el pollo y sirva.

title: Ensalada de Rúcula con Mandarinas
description: El sabor pimentoso de la rúcula pequeña combina bien con el tocino dulce, fresco, cítrico y crujiente en esta ensalada acompañante. La rúcula es un vegetal sin almidón que está llena de nutrientes. ¡Cada taza solo tiene 5 calorías y 1 gramo de carbohidratos junto con 10% de vitamina A recomendada por día y 25% de vitamina K recomendada por día! Encuentra esta receta y más en el Libro de recetas para diabéticos. Para pedirlo directamente de la American Diabetes Association, haz clic aquí.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 160; Grasa Total 12g 15%; Grasa Saturada 2g 10%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 5mg 2%; Sodio 150mg 7%; Carbohidratos Totales 12g 4%; Fibra dietética 2g 7%; Azúcares totales 9g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 4g; Potasio 280mg 6%
ingredients: 3 tbsp Aceite de oliva virgen extra
steps: En una ensaladera, mezcla la rúcula, tocino, y los segmentos de la naranja.
En un tazón pequeño, bate el jugo de naranja, ralladura de naranja, aceite de oliva, pimienta, y estragón. Vierte el aderezo sobre la ensalada y revuelve para cubrirla.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Camarones envueltos en Tocino
description:
No te sorprendas cuando estos aperitivos sean devorados en tu próxima fiesta. ¡Este clásico plato de camarones prueba que algunas veces las recetas más sencillas son las complacientes de multitudes!

Encuentra esta receta y más en el Libro de recetas para diabéticos. Para pedirlo directamente a la Asociación Americana de la Diabetes, haz clic aquí.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 70; Grasa Total 2.5g 3%; Grasa Saturada 1g 5%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 85mg 28%; Sodio 380mg 17%; Carbohidratos Totales 0g 0%; Fibra dietética 0g 0%; Azúcares totales 0g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 11g; Potasio 120mg 3%
ingredients: 20 large camarón (jumbo size, peeled and deveined)
steps: Precalienta la parrilla.
Corta cada rebanada tocino en diagonal en tres piezas. Envuelve una pieza alrededor de cada camarón. Colócalos en una bandeja para hornear y asa por 2-3 minutos por lado, volteando una vez.
Sirve los camarones sobre las hojas de lechuga.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Chef Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: "Helado" de Banana y Chocolate
description: Es difícil de creer, pero las bananas congeladas constituyen una estupenda base para este "helado" suave de cuatro ingredientes, que es bajo en grasas saturadas. Compra pequeños moldes de pastelería o tazas para facilitar el control de porciones cuando sirvas postre como este.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 80; Grasa Total 0g 0%; Grasa Saturada 0g 0%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 0mg 0%; Sodio 15mg <1%; Carbohidratos Totales 18g 7%; Fibra dietética 2g 7%; Azúcares totales 8g; Azúcares añadidos 2g 4%; Proteína 1g; Potasio 202mg 4%
steps: Pela las bananas y rebánalas en monedas de 1/4 de pulgada. Colócalas en un tazón y congélalas durante al menos 2 horas.
Una vez que las bananas estén congeladas, añade las bananas, leche, y cacao en polvo a la licuadora. Licuar hasta que quede sin grumos.
Incorpora la crema batida.
Coloca la mezcla en un recipiente apto para el congelador y congélala durante al menos 30 minutos.
Echa la mezcla en cucharadas de 1/2 taza para servir.

title: Hummus de Frijoles Negros
description: ¿Por qué detenerse en garbanzos? Añadir los frijoles negros y añade un poco de comino para una nueva versión del hummus. Sirve con palitos de vegetales frescos para sumergir.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 90; Grasa Total 3g 4%; Grasa Saturada 0g 0%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 0mg 0%; Sodio 85mg 4%; Carbohidratos Totales 12g 4%; Fibra dietética 4g 14%; Azúcares totales 2g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 4g; Potasio 300mg 6%
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can frijoles negros (low sodium, rinsed and drained)
steps: Coloca todos los ingredientes en un procesador de alimentos y licúa hasta que quede sin grumos. Añadir más agua si la consistencia es demasiado espesa.

title: Ensalada abundante de Vegetales de Cosecha
description: Esta es una forma maravillosa de usar productos frescos desde la primera cosecha hasta la última. El contraste del aderezo caliente, vegetales cocidos tiernos, y los crujientes rábanos y nueces sobre los vegetales verdes es un banquete para tus pupilas gustativas. ¡Y esta ensalada está llena de nutrientes para tu cuerpo!
nutrients_raw: Calorías 150; Grasa Total 9g 12%; Grasa Saturada 1g 5%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 0mg 0%; Sodio 110mg 5%; Carbohidratos Totales 16g 6%; Fibra dietética 4g 14%; Azúcares totales 6g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 3g; Potasio 470mg 10%
steps: Pon a hervir una olla con agua salada. Añadir las chirivías y los nabos y cocina a fuego lento hasta que los vegetales estén tiernos, por 8-10 minutos. Escurre bien.

Mientras que las chirivías y nabos se están cocinando, elabora el aderezo. Calienta el aceite en una sartén grande a fuego medio. Añadir las cebollas y cocina hasta que estén doradas, por 5-7 minutos. Añadir el ajo y cocina durante 30 segundos más. Incorpora el vinagre y el azúcar y lleva la mezcla a una cocción a fuego lento. Retira del fuego y mantén el aderezo caliente.
Acomoda el perejil, cilantro, y ensalada de verduras y cúbrelos con vegetales calientes, luego decora con nueces y rábano. Rocía con el aderezo tibio, y sirve inmediatamente.
credits: Origen: The Budget-Friendly Fresh and Local Diabetes Cookbook

title: Hinojo estofado con judías blancas
description: Acompaña estas alubias estofadas con hinojo con una guarnición de pollo para disfrutar de una comida completa y reconfortante.
serving_size: 3 trozos de hinojo, 1/3 taza de frijoles y salsa
nutrients_raw: Calorías 140; Grasa Total 3g 4%; Grasa Saturada 0g 0%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 0mg 0%; Sodio 270mg 12%; Carbohidratos Totales 23g 8%; Fibra dietética 7g 25%; Azúcares totales 4g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 6g; Potasio 690mg 15%
ingredients: 2 medium bulbo de hinojo (Aproximadamente 312 gramos cada una, sin tallos ni hojas, cortadas en octavos.)
1 taza caldo de pollo bajo en sodio (sin grasa, bajo en sodio)
15.5 ounces, 1 can frijoles cannellini (escurrido y enjuagado)
steps: Precaliente el horno a 190 °C (375 °F). Rocíe un molde para hornear de 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 pulgadas) con aceite en aerosol.
Coloca el hinojo y la cebolla en el fondo de la fuente para hornear preparada.
Vierta el aceite de oliva, el caldo y el vinagre sobre el hinojo y la cebolla, y sazone con sal y pimienta.
Hornear durante 1 hora, removiendo a la mitad del tiempo.
Añade las judías verdes y el perejil y vuelve a meterlo en el horno durante 10 minutos.

title: Albóndigas de arroz integral estofadas
description: Esta receta de albóndigas es un excelente complemento para una comida sustanciosa. Acompáñala con una guarnición de verduras y tendrás una combinación insuperable.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 200; Grasa Total 5g 6%; Grasa Saturada 2g 10%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 80mg 27%; Sodio 190mg 8%; Carbohidratos Totales 20g 7%; Fibra dietética 2g 7%; Azúcares totales 4g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 18g; Potasio 440mg 9%
ingredients: 16 oz jugo de vegetales (bajo en sodio)
steps: Precalentar el horno a 350 °F.
Añade todos los ingredientes, excepto el jugo de verduras, a un bol y mezcla bien. Forma 12 albóndigas con la mezcla.
Coloca las albóndigas en una fuente pequeña para hornear, añade el jugo de verduras y hornea durante 30 minutos.
Si lo desea, sírvalo con una ensalada verde aliñada con un poco de aceite de oliva y zumo de limón.

title: Arroz frito de coliflor
description: La coliflor finamente picada puede ser una guarnición sin almidón excepcional, con menos calorías y carbohidratos que el arroz. También puedes convertirla en plato principal añadiéndole pechuga de pollo, camarones o tofu. Para simplificar aún más esta receta, usa coliflor rallada envasada, que puedes encontrar fresca o congelada en muchos supermercados.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 80; Grasa Total 5g 6%; Grasa Saturada 1g 5%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 0mg 0%; Sodio 280mg 12%; Carbohidratos Totales 9g 3%; Fibra dietética 3g 11%; Azúcares totales 4g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 2g; Potasio 420mg 9%
ingredients: 1/4 taza caldo de pollo bajo en sodio (Sin sal añadida, sin grasa)
steps: Corta la coliflor en trozos pequeños y procésala en un procesador de alimentos hasta obtener una consistencia similar al arroz, o ralla la cabeza de coliflor con un rallador; reserva.
Calienta 1/2 cucharada de aceite de oliva en una sartén antiadherente a fuego medio-alto. Agrega las zanahorias y las cebolletas y sofríe durante 5 minutos.

Añade la media cucharada restante de aceite de oliva y el aceite de sésamo a la sartén. Agrega el “arroz” de coliflor y el resto de los ingredientes y baja el fuego a medio-bajo. Cocina la mezcla de coliflor durante 6-8 minutos, removiendo con frecuencia. La coliflor debe quedar tierna, pero no blanda.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Cassoulet de Pollo y Frijoles
description: ¿Quieres un alimento reconfortante para invierno? ¡Prueba el cassoulet! Esta receta para una cacerola francesa en olla de cocción lenta reemplaza los ingredientes tradicionales de cerdo y pato con kielbasa de pavo y muslos de pollo. Nota: Esta comida es ligeramente alta en sodio, así que aquellos que estén en una dieta baja en sodio ajusten su plan de alimentación en consecuencia.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 200; Grasa Total 8g 10%; Grasa Saturada 2g 10%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 95mg 32%; Sodio 420mg 18%; Carbohidratos Totales 9g 3%; Fibra dietética 3g 11%; Azúcares totales 2g; Azúcares añadidos 0g 0%; Proteína 22g; Potasio 400mg 9%
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs (Cut into 8 large pieces if 8 pieces don’t equal 1 1/2 lb)
1 1/2 taza caldo de pollo bajo en sodio
15 ounces, 1 can frijoles cannellini (drained and rinsed)
steps: Añadir el aceite en aerosol a una cazuela grande a fuego alto. Condimenta el pollo por ambos lados con sal y pimienta. Sella el pollo por ambos lados hasta que esté dorado, aproximadamente 5 minutos, luego retíralo de la cacerola y reserva.
Baja el fuego a medio. Añadir la kielbasa y saltéala por 3 minutos. Retíralo de la sartén y reserva.

Añadir la cebolla, ajo y zanahorias. Saltea durante 3-4 minutos, luego añade la pasta de tomate, tomillo y caldo de pollo. Raspa los bocados marrones del fondo de la cacerola y llévala a ebullición. Reduce a una cocción a fuego lento, luego añade el pollo y salchicha de vuelta a la cacerola con cualquier jugo acumulado. Tapa y cocina a fuego lento por 8 minutos. Retira la tapa y cocina a fuego lento por 5 minutos. Retira el pollo y reserva.
Añadir los frijoles. Cambia el fuego a alto. Cocina a fuego lento por 5 minutos más hasta que el líquido esté ligeramente reducido. Retira los tallos del tomillo.
Para servir, coloca un muslo de pollo en el fondo del tazón, y vierte 1/2 taza del estofado sobre él.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: berenjena parmesano
description: Sí, puedes preparar berenjenas con queso y crujientes que le encantarán a toda la familia, ¡con cereales integrales y sin freír! Sirva con ensalada verde y pasta integral para una comida completa. Para una opción baja en carbohidratos, use fideos de calabacín o espaguetis en lugar de pasta.
nutrients_raw: Calorías 150; Grasa Total 6g 8%; Grasa Saturada 1.2g 6%; Grasas Trans 0g; Colesterol 5mg 2%; Sodio 240mg 10%; Carbohidratos Totales 20g 7%; Fibra dietética 3g 11%; Azúcares totales 5g; Proteína 6g; Potasio 320mg 7%
ingredients: 1 medium (about 1 lb) berenjena (cortado en rodajas de 10 1/2 pulgadas de grosor)
1 (24-oz) jar salsa marinara reducida en sodio
steps: Precalienta el horno a 350°F.
En un tazón mediano, combine la harina, la albahaca y la pimienta. En otro tazón mediano, combine el pan rallado y el queso parmesano. En un tercer tazón mediano, agrega las claras de huevo.
Pase ambos lados de las rodajas de berenjena por harina, luego por huevos y luego por pan rallado, cubriendo bien. Dejar de lado.

Agregue aceite y aceite en aerosol a una sartén antiadherente grande a fuego medio-alto. Cocine las berenjenas en tandas, aproximadamente 2 minutos por lado. Use spray para cocinar adicional con cada lote.

Coloque las rodajas de berenjena en el fondo de una fuente para hornear de 13x9 pulgadas. Vierta la salsa para pasta sobre la berenjena para cubrir todas las rebanadas. Espolvoree queso mozzarella por encima y hornee por 30 minutos, hasta que el queso se derrita y esté ligeramente dorado.
credits: Recipe by: Lara Rondinelli Hamilton, RD, LDN, CDE and Jennifer Bucko Lamplough

title: Tofu General Tso con brócoli
description: ¿Comida china sin tener que pedir a domicilio? Es posible preparar platos deliciosos con un bajo contenido de sodio y calorías.
